News.title: George Russell king of the sprint and driving with freedom after engagement
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the sprint race for the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix, the first race after F1’s summer break. Kimi Antonelli has had a tremendous first part of the season, leading Lewis Hamilton by 50 points and George Russell by 59 after the first 11 rounds. He has taken six wins to Russell’s two, with Hamilton, Lando Norris and Charles Leclerc all racking up a win apiece.

His start to the second part of the season was not the best, however. A messy sprint qualifying session meant he ended down in fifth, more than 0.2sec behind team-mate Russell, who took a much-needed pole.

Some of the damage was self-inflicted, quite literally. In the first session of sprint qualifying he ran wide at the banked turn 12 and into the gravel. The damage to the floor of his car was attempted to be repaired for the rest of the session but left him lacking downforce. A gap of 0.2sec is not enormous but the other issue was that three other cars – Norris, Leclerc and Piastri – are between him and Russell.

That said, it is not a great worry at this point. The points available in the sprint are relatively small and Antonelli has a healthy margin at this point over his rivals. In any case, there is no guarantee that Russell and Antonelli finish where they will start. Antonelli has shown on numerous occasions that he can bounce back from a difficult session and you have to expect that again here.

The race, which starts at 11am BST, is one-third of the race distance and should be run in dry conditions. There have been persistent showers and a steady breeze at Zandvoort this weekend, but it is not expected to affect the running in the sprint.

Qualifying for tomorrow’s grand prix comes later today at 3pm, which could be a more consequential session.

News.title: Arsenal play like the champions they are as title defence starts with a bang
News.content:
Good evening and welcome to the Emirates Stadium, where the Premier League champions begin the defence of their title. Or, as Mikel Arteta prefers to put it, their “attack” on a new season. A classic Arteta-ism.

The assault starts tonight against Coventry City but our understanding is that Arsenal will be without new £75m midfielder Bruno Guimaraes. We believe the Brazilian has picked up an injury, and it’s not currently clear how severe it might be. Clearly, this is a blow for Arteta. But they should still have enough to get past promoted Coventry… shouldn’t they? We’ll find out soon enough.

Meanwhile, Arteta has said he and his players should relish being Premier League title favourites and the role of the hunted rather than the hunter.

“In the last three seasons, at some point we were first and at some point we were chasing. And you never know what is better,” Arteta said. “But if you give me the choice, I want to be first. I want to be hunted, and I want to be in control of our future, rather than depending on somebody else.”

Arteta called on his players to retain the hunger they had last season.

“We start from scratch, from zero, and we’re going to have to prove we are at the level to go back to that position again,” he said. “We need to show that desire and the ambition to be better than what we were last season, a month ago, a week ago.”

This is Coventry’s first Premier League campaign since they suffered relegation in 2000-01, and they were led to the Championship title by Frank Lampard. They scored the most goals in the Championship and conceded the fewest, and could face one of their former players tonight in Viktor Gyokeres.

Full team news as and when we get it.

News.title: Russell takes Dutch GP sprint pole as Antonelli struggles to fifth
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for sprint qualifying for the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix from Zandvoort. This is the last time the race will be on the F1 calendar for the foreseeable future, having been reintroduced in 2021 after a 35-year absence. It will be a shame to see it leave again, but never rule out it coming back, especially with Max Verstappen signing a lengthy contract extension with Red Bull.

What of the competitive action this weekend? As it is a sprint weekend, there is not a lot of preparation time, with just one practice session before sprint qualifying. In that it was a fairly close fight at the top, and it was Kimi Antonelli, the championship leader, who was fastest of all. Behind him was the McLaren of Lando Norris who was 0.121sec adrift then George Russell, who will be looking to kickstart his title campaign here, a further 0.004sec behind him.

Then came the two Ferraris of Lewis Hamilton (0.190sec) and Charles Leclerc (0.289sec) before a fairly significant gap of 0.659sec to Oscar Piastri in sixth. Verstappen was down in 11th, nearly 1.4sec off Antonelli’s ultimate pace but 0.5sec or so ahead of new (and old) team-mate for the weekend, Liam Lawson.

It was a tricky session for the drivers, though, as it began damp on a showery and blustery day by the Dutch seaside. Several drivers ran wide and off the track, though they all avoided anything more serious than gravel rash. The rest of the day looks to be drier but there are still a few showers around and the wind is all over the place, as it often is here.

Sprint qualifying starts at 3.30pm BST and we will be here for all of the updates for the nearly hour-long session.

News.title: Root delivers perfect riposte to captaincy doubters as England hammer Pakistan
News.content:
There was no attempt to be a Ben Stokes tribute act by Joe Root, just a measured captaincy performance very much in his own undemonstrative style.

Root, ever the team man, pushed his bowlers forward to lead England off at the end, recognising the match-winners in a walkover against Pakistan, who were bowled out for 135 in under two sessions.

Victory by an innings and 103 runs inside three days marked a perfect return to the job and put the smile back on England faces for the first time in a long while. The chants of “F--- the ECB” from Trent Bridge, after the New Zealand regime-toppling loss, were replaced by the Yorkshire faithful’s “Roooot”.

There was plenty of scepticism around rebooting the Root captaincy, but he was the only realistic choice. Harry Brook’s batting here was more sensible and at a tempo in the captain’s mould. “He is still learning the art of Test cricket,” Root said. Thrusting Brook into the job would have put more pressure on him, he may well have felt he needed to make risky statements with the bat. Now he can mature under Root and Stephen Fleming.

Tactically, Root was astute and showed enough to suggest he is going to be different this time. The old Root would not have whipped Jofra Archer off after two overs of the Test, but it was a prod that worked as he bowled quicker and more accurately to strike twice with the second-innings new ball, using his new-found skills with a scrambled seam to good effect.

It also showed his bowlers he wanted a fuller length and, from that first hour, they controlled the match and did not let their grip slip.

Root promised to keep the good aspects of Bazball and apply common sense. He continued Stokes’s leg-slip tactic and it paid off with the wicket of opener Azan Awais, and urged Ollie Robinson to bowl with the keeper standing up. England batted at 4.5 an over – a touch quicker than the Bazball years – but it was never reckless, just a calm tempo, with no ramps or scoops.

News.title: Officials selling yellow fever certificates to unvaccinated travellers
News.content:
Officials in Malawi are selling yellow fever certificates to unvaccinated travellers for around $20 and sending them on their way, a Telegraph investigation has found.



The passport-sized, yellow document, officially called the International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (ICVP), is supposed to provide proof of vaccination against yellow fever, a mosquito-borne virus that kills tens of thousands of people every year.

The jab provides lifelong protection, beginning 10 days after vaccination. Most countries in Africa and Latin America require them for entry, either for all travellers or for those arriving from risk areas.



Yet travellers leaving Malawi through two major airports can get hold of the certificates without ever being vaccinated, according to interviews with multiple travellers and an undercover investigation.



Several passengers who travelled recently from Malawi to destinations including Uganda, Kenya, Ethiopia and China said they had obtained yellow fever vaccination certificates at airports or public hospitals without receiving the vaccine.



One traveller, who recently flew to Uganda for work from Kamuzu International Airport, which serves the capital, Lilongwe, said he was initially told it was too late to get vaccinated because his departure was less than 10 days away.



“When I asked the health officials if I could get vaccinated at the airport, I was told it was too late because I needed to be vaccinated ten days before my trip,” he told The Telegraph.



“But then they offered to arrange the certificate for me for roughly $21,” said the traveller, who asked not to be named. “I had to pay because I could not postpone the trip.”

News.title: Congo gambles on ‘old’ vaccine as new Ebola virus spirals
News.content:
Nearly half of all those infected have gone on to die.

Dr Sania Nishtar, chief executive of the Gavi global vaccine partnership, earlier this week said to beat the outbreak “we must deploy every tool at our disposal”.

She went on: “To avoid this becoming the worst recorded Ebola outbreak in history, it is critical that all effective countermeasure options are brought to bear.

“We have a tool that could help save lives while we wait for [Bundibugyo]-specific vaccines to become available.”

Previous clinical trials have shown that Ervebo is safe, but its effect on other strains is unknown.

The World Health Organisation said in a statement that while it was not known if Ervebo may protect against the Bundibugyo virus, “early laboratory and animal data suggest it may provide some protection”.

Medics told the Telegraph of anecdotal claims that health workers who had been given Ervebo to protect them during an outbreak of the Zaire strain in 2018 to 2020 had not fallen ill during the current Bundibugyo outbreak.

Health workers are at extreme risk of catching the disease because they come into contact with highly-contagious blood, vomit and diarrhoea from dying patients. When they fall sick themselves, they frequently go on to infect their own families.

Giving health workers vaccine jabs to protect them as they tend the sick is a cornerstone of Ebola responses.

The WHO said the vaccine allocation includes 20,000 doses for a Phase 3 clinical trial to understand the impact of the vaccine on the Bundibugyo virus. The remaining 50,000 doses will be used for front-line and health workers as recommended by WHO experts.

Dr Nishtar said: “Having already been licensed for the Zaire strain, we know that Ervebo is proven to be safe.

“And while the signs are that it may not stop transmission – which is essential for ending the outbreak - it could well save precious lives and reduce suffering.”

Health officials warn that the Bundibugyo outbreak centred on DRC’s Ituri province is easily outpacing relief efforts.

The virus is thought to have been spreading for months before an outbreak was finally declared in mid-May and medics have been unable to make up the head start.

An analysis by the Africa Centres for Disease Control meanwhile warned the current outbreak dwarfed all others on record

The current outbreak had almost ten times more cases than any other previous outbreak at a similar stage.

News.title: Soaring welfare bill pushes national debt to almost £3tn
News.content:
Britain’s soaring welfare bill forced John Healey to borrow more to balance the books last month.

The gap between tax receipts and spending unexpectedly resulted in a £1.8bn deficit in July, taking the national debt to within a whisker of £3tn.

Economists had predicted the Government would borrow nothing and blamed the deficit on the rising welfare bill.

Figures published by the Office for National Statistics (ONS) this morning show total debt rose to £2.985tn in July.

Benefit payments also climbed by 7.2pc, or £2bn, to £30bn last month.

The Chancellor now faces another tax-raising Budget in October, even as strong receipts from self-employed workers provide some respite.

The ONS also said Mr Healey spent £7.7bn on debt interest in July alone, almost 10pc higher than a year ago.

Ashley Webb, at Capital Economics said: “The weak performance was mainly due higher social payments.”

Monthly borrowing was slightly higher than the Office for Budget Responsibility and markets expected, meaning the Government has borrowed £56.7bn this financial year to plug the gap between tax receipts and public spending.

Julian Jessop, an independent economist and IEA economics fellow, said: “The latest official data highlight the fragility of the public finances as John Healey prepares his first Budget. Government borrowing was £2.3bn above forecast in July, and £0.7bn higher than in the same month a year ago.”

July is traditionally a strong month for receipts from the self-employed, with self-assessed income tax receipts last month coming to £17.1bn, about £1.7bn more than a year earlier.

However, higher inflation triggered by the Iran war means Mr Healey will be forced to use the Budget to find billions of pounds to repair the public finances.

Mr Healey said: “Fiscal discipline is the bedrock of our UK economic stability and national security which is why we are committed to meeting our fiscal rules, with a buffer against global uncertainties.”

The Resolution Foundation warned that the Chancellor’s headroom against his fiscal rules - self-imposed guardrails to guide public spending - has shrunk from around £24bn in the Spring Statement to less than £8bn today.

The think tank called on the Chancellor to use his first Budget on Oct 28 to put the nation’s finances on a more sustainable path.

Elliott Christensen, senior economist at the Resolution Foundation, said: “The Chancellor’s margin against his fiscal rules is now razor thin.”

Sports.title: Man Utd legend Peter Schmeichel slams two ‘sloppy’ stars for shambolic moment in humiliating Hull defeat
Sports.content:
PETER SCHMEICHEL has slammed Patrick Dorgu and Ayden Heaven for their role in Manchester United’s shambolic defending during their humiliating defeat to Hull City.

The Red Devils legend was left furious after United conceded twice in the first half of their 2-0 loss at the MKM Stadium.



Newly-promoted Hull stunned Michael Carrick‘s side as Semi Ajayi smashed home the opener from close range after United failed to properly deal with a corner.

Former United keeper Schmeichel wasted no time picking out Dorgu and Heaven for their roles in the sloppy defending.



Analysing the goal at half-time on Premier League Productions, the Dane said: “This is sloppy defending, this is all about concentrating.

“Look at Dorgu, Dorgu on the front post, he is not even looking at the guy taking the corner kick.”

“At that exact moment, he loses his concentration, he does not have the ability to block the first ball.”

Dorgu’s lapse allowed the ball to reach the danger area, with United unable to clear their lines before Ajayi pounced.

Schmeichel added: “And of course, Ayden Heaven on the back post. That’s not how you defend, you have to be stronger.”

Debutant Nobel Mendy headed home the second to leave the hosts 2-0 up and United facing a mountain to climb – something they didn’t manage to do.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

It was a brutal assessment from Schmeichel, who won five Premier League titles while at United during the 90s.

United also won the Champions League in 1998/99 on a night where Schmeichel captained the side in the absence of the suspended Roy Keane.

He played under the same manager throughout in Sir Alex Ferguson, who once famously said: “Attack wins you games, defence wins you titles.”

That was certainly the case in the 90s while Schmeichel was playing in net, and in front of him he regularly had a solid defence.



The likes of Gary and Phil Neville, Gary Pallister, Steve Bruce, Denis Irwin, Jaap Stam and Ronny Johnsen formed the base of consistent title winning teams.

That’s why today’s under par defensive performance from the Red Devils would have angered Schmeichel even more as it’s something he wasn’t used to during his playing days at the club.

United had never previously lost their opening league fixture of a season against a newly-promoted team, winning nine and drawing three of their previous 12 meetings.

But for Hull, today is a day that will live long in the memory on Humberside.

Sports.title: Fans cringe as Sky Sports commentators make ‘dad jokes’ after cameras pan to Jon Bon Jovi in crowd for Brentford-Spurs
Sports.content:
FOOTBALL fans were left cringing as Sky Sports commentators made dad jokes after spotting Jon Bon Jovi at Brentford vs Tottenham.

The music icon was sitting in the crowd at the Gtech when cameras panned to him in black sunnies.



Smiling away, the American, 64, was quickly the subject of some song puns.

With Bill Leslie on main duties and Alan Smith his co-comms partner, the pair immediately cracked a gag.



Leslie said: “There was a rumour doing the rounds that he’d come to watch one of Tottenham’s new signings that he heard had joined from a coastal club.

“He heard that Jonny used to work down the docks.”

Referencing the lyrics from top hit Livin’ on a Prayer, Smith picked up on it and replied: “It’s been a Bed of Roses for Spurs so far.”

That drew a laugh from Leslie but fans weren’t sure about their chat.

One wrote online: “The pre written Bon Jovi gags a new low”.

Others were happier to see the legend in attendance.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

A different user said: “Oh my god lads (Spurs) you CANNOT embarrass me Infront of THE Jon Bon Jovi!!!!”

Someone else commented: “spurs opening premier league game & my commentators are making bon jovi jokes. we are so back”.

And many were just confused.

An account questioned: “John Bon Jovi is at Brentford for the game against Tottenham. Wonder what team he supports.”

Bon Jovi is due to play three nights at Wembley on his Forever tour early next month.

Sports.title: Non-league side slam ref for refusing to call off FA Cup game with pitch ‘unplayable’ – fans say ‘genuinely disgusting’
Sports.content:
NON-LEAGUE club Beckenham Town have slammed a “disgraceful” referee after he deemed a pitch playable, despite it being in a shocking state.

The club have vowed to get in touch with the FA, after the ref gave the go ahead on an “absolutely awful” pitch.



The club posted a video of the turf, or lack of, at FA Cup opponents Camberley Town on their X account, while slamming the ref in the process.

They said: “Absolutely disgraceful decision by the referee, I don’t think he’s qualified enough to call this game on.



“The pitch is absolutely awful, you can’t see the goal areas, you can’t see the markings.”

They added that they plan to contact the FA to find out which ref gave the pitch the go-ahead the day before.

Beckenham went on to lose in dramatic fashion on the barren surface, throwing away a 2-1 lead to eventually lose 3-2.

It means their FA Cup dream is over for another season, but they will feel hard-done-by, after being forced to play on the arid pitch.

Fans also had their say on social media, as the clip went viral.

One wrote: “That is genuinely disgusting.”



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Another one hilariously compared it to the Star Wars sand planet Tattooine.

While a third posted: “Games will get called off for frozen pitches but they allow them to be played on these concrete dustbowls.”

Sports.title: ‘Goal of the season already’ – EFL star scores Puskas contender with outrageous backheeled volley into top bins
Sports.content:
BRISTOL CITY striker Dom Ballard scored a Puskas Award contender in the late stages of a Championship thriller against Birmingham.

The 21-year-old sent a backheeled volley flying into the top-left corner in the 85th minute of the match to put City 2-1 up at St Andrew’s.

Ballard pounced onto a cross from Rio Cardines with his back to goal and flicked his right boot at the ball, firing it past James Beadle and into the Birmingham net.



Fans were quick to react on social media, with one person writing: “DOM BALLARD THAT IS GOAL OF THE SEASON ALREADY!”



Another commented: “DOM BALLARD that is INSANE, goal of the season is already in boys and girls!”

A third wrote: “What on earth has Dom Ballard just done… Goal of the season already.”

While a fourth said: “Dom Ballard, this is magical.”



Despite the incredible finish, Bristol City went on to concede a 95th-minute equaliser from Demarai Gray.

Speaking after the match, Ballard said: “Not just me, the performance is from everyone.

“Everyone played their role today and did it really well.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“But yeah, to score that goal, I don’t think I’ll score many better.



“Really, really happy.”

Ballard’s stunning strike was his first competitive goal for Bristol City since completing his move from Leyton Orient earlier this month.

Sports.title: ‘Which numpty signed off on this?’ – Fans baffled by bizarre kit clash in Tottenham’s Premier League visit to Brentford
Sports.content:
TOTTENHAM fans have been left baffled over a bizarre kit clash for their opening day trip to Brentford.

Spurs travelled to the Gtech on Saturday sporting their unusual navy away kit with purple, orange and blue diagonal stripes.



But it didn’t mesh too well with Brentford‘s home kit, which uses red and white stripes.

And supporters voiced their frustrations on X as they called the clash “annoying”.



One Spurs fan wrote: “Which numpty signed off on using this kit when today? This is one hell of clash with Brentford’s at least on tv viewing anyway.”

Another said: “What’s going on with this kit clash very annoying.”



A third added: “The kit clash is still present today… should’ve worn the home kit.”

And a fourth said: “Bit of a kit clash?”

The clash wasn’t the only thing troubling Spurs fans as they watched their side go 1-0 down in the opening 12 minutes.

Keane Lewis-Potter was left totally unmarked inside the box and calmly dispatched.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

And the Bees made it 2-0 midway through the first half as Vitaly Janelt buried a rebound after Lucas Bergvall‘s error.

It was shock to the system for Tottenham, who had been backed for a big season under Robeto De Zerbi after spending nearly £300million this summer.

Spurs started the game with new signings Andy Robetson, Marcos Senesi, Jan Paul van Hecke and Sandro Tonali.

But the north London outfit barely created any chances in the first half as Brentford frustrated them.

Tottenham were hoping to put their disaster 2025-26 campaign behind them after scraping survival on the final day with just 41 points.

Sports.title: Arsenal superstar Bukayo Saka shrugs off World Cup heartbreak and injury agony with secret seven-day fitness regime
Sports.content:
BUKAYO SAKA could be forgiven for starting this season slowly and with a World Cup hangover.

The winger endured a frustrating tournament and his hat-trick in England’s third-place play-off win over France came in only a third start.



But there were no lingering signs of that disappointment — nor the Achilles issue that had dogged Saka since March – on Friday night.

He was electric and scored Arsenal’s second goal as the champions began their title defence with a convincing 3-0 win over Coventry.



For Saka, 24, it was reward for his hard work during a short break, where he learned the best tonic for any hangover is getting a sweat on.

The winger said: “I was training a lot so I could be ready for the start of the season — and ready to help the team in the way I know I can.

“It was more about balancing my time off and not having too much of a break. I took seven days off and then started to train again.

“I’ve put in a lot of work since then and I’m feeling good. I just tried to come back in good shape, so I’m on top of my body.

“The World Cup didn’t necessarily go how I wanted it to – for myself and for the team as well.

“I felt really hungry after the World Cup, after the season ended. I was looking forward to this new season.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

There had been suspicions Gunners boss Mikel Arteta would look to ease Saka back into action this season.

But the winger put paid to that by returning to training a few days early and expressing his desire to get going.

The end result is that Arsenal’s attack has looked sharp in their first two games of the season.

A 3-0 win over Manchester City in the Community Shield last Sunday was followed with another three goals against Prem new boys Coventry.



The Gunners looked sluggish going forward on their way to winning the Prem last term but early signs suggest their title defence will be different.

Saka and captain Martin Odegaard have rekindled the connection that makes them so dangerous – and suddenly the attack is flowing.

Odegaard scored Arsenal’s third on Friday night and the first came courtesy of Kai Havertz, who also adds to the team’s fluency.

Just like Saka, a fit Odegaard has made a huge difference and the pair will take some stopping on this form.



Saka added: “Martin is playing really well. Last week against City he played really well, got his goal and he has done the same again.

“When he plays well, the team is just a lot better. And this was a great start for the team.

“We played beautiful football and scored the goals the game required.”

Saka caught the eye against Frank Lampard’s Sky Blues – but Christos Tzolis on the opposite flank was just as impressive.

The winger has hit the ground running since moving from Club Brugge in the summer for £34million.



Tzolis, 24, had a hand in Saka’s goal as it was his cross that Coventry goalkeeper Carl Rushworth spilled to the England star’s feet.

It capped off a stunning home debut for the Greek – and he is quickly becoming a fan favourite.

Arsenal remain in the market for a new left winger after missing out on both Morgan Rogers and Vinicius Jr this summer but all-action Tzolis has shown that he is ready to step up.

He said: “There was a lot of excitement when I had the ball and that gave me motivation to have confidence in my actions.”



Arteta also played down fears over fellow new boy Bruno Guimaraes’ fitness.

The Brazilian midfielder – a £75m buy from Newcastle – missed the Prem opener with a groin issue.

But asked if he could be out for weeks, Arteta replied: “No, no. We don’t expect that. Let’s see how he evolves this week.”

Sports.title: Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos show Michael Carrick why Man Utd desperately need Carlos Baleba after stinker vs Hull
Sports.content:
ANDREY SANTOS and Youri Tielemans put the mid in midfield as Manchester United stunk the place out against Hull – and that is being generous.

Michael Carrick‘s new-look pairing were completely ineffective behind Bruno Fernandes and left much to be desired in an embarrassing 2-0 loss.



The opening day competitive debuts for each went terribly as they were hooked after 67 minutes.

In a minor positive, neither Kobbie Mainoo nor Benjamin Sesko had any more luck after coming on, and nobody else had any luck for United.



But with the club still looking to buy a THIRD midfielder of the window, Brighton may well be thinking about bumping up their asking price for Carlos Baleba.

A deal worth around £65million for the player has been agreed but United are so desperate in the centre of the park that they would surely settle for paying even more at this stage.



Historic tough negotiators, Brighton could ask United to throw money at them for Baleba and little argument would surely be put up, he is that big of an addition.

Where Santos and Tielemans were short against Hull, Baleba drives from deep and covers ground for fun.

He is a wide-ranging passer and explosive in marauding across the pitch.

None of those words could be used to describe United’s £85million pair on Humberside.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Santos, who cost £50million of that figure from Chelsea, had been one of the standout performers in pre-season.

He and Mason Mount, another ex-Blue costing £65million, impressed on tour.

But at newly promoted – and massive favourites to go straight back down – Hull, he was stunted.

Brazilian Santos may well have completed 52 of his 56 passes (93 per cent) but almost half of those were safely in his own half.

He lost the ball FIVE times and only produced one progressive carry despite Hull sitting on the edge of their own penalty area.



Usually an adventurous line-breaker, Santos couldn’t impact the game at all.

He committed one foul and ended up making more clearances (three) than chances.

If Santos stumbled then Tielemans fell flat on his face.

The Belgian, a £35million signing from Aston Villa, was even worse.



Another player used to advancing play in possession, he misplaced EIGHT passes and completed less than 50 per cent of his 62 in Hull’s half.

He lost the ball FIVE times trying to get it forward in the middle third and was a hinderance when travelling with it.

Hull nabbed the ball off him on 11 occasions and made light work of getting past him when attacking.

Tielemans made one foul, was dribbled past twice, and made ZERO defensive contributions.



Even Baleba, coming off the back of a tough year on the south coast, will be able to offer more impetus.

And Carrick best hope that it moves along quickly as he seeks to get United going.

Sports.title: Furious Man Utd skipper Bruno Fernandes rips into team-mates for ‘same mistakes’ after horror opening day defeat to Hull
Sports.content:
BRUNO FERNANDES slammed Manchester United for failing to learn from their “mistakes in every away game”.

The United skipper blasted the lack of “aggression” in the Red Devils’ horror 2-0 Prem opening defeat at newly promoted Hull City.



Hull scored twice from set pieces in the first half to record a first ever Prem victory over United.

United dominated the possession but barely created anything, with Bryan Mbeumo seeing two efforts comfortably saved.



United captain Fernandes, who reopened contract talks with Ineos this week, cut a frustrated figure as he lambasted the lack of fight.

The 31-year-old told TNT Sports: “Same mistakes as we did last season, every away game we give too much of the ball to them,



“In the first 20 minutes, the goalkeeper was the one with the most touches.

“We needed to press more, be more aggressive, and then again we need to work on set-plays and not concede these types of goals. Against these types of teams, they are waiting for that moment.

“We knew before the game set-pieces would be a big part of their game. They played all pre-season with a back four but had a five against us for some height, for these moments. The most frustrating thing is that we lost the game.”

He added: “We knew how motivated they would be. If someone didn’t know, it’s very surprising. We know in the Premier League these types of grounds are very difficult to play in.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“You need to match everything in intensity, aggression and everything. We had that apart from two set pieces. That cost us the game.

“I understand the frustration. Every season that starts, we want to compete and go as forward as we can, winning every game. We need them on our side, like last season, believing in us. We know we need more from ourselves too.”

It was the first game of Carrick’s tenure as United’s permanent manager and he remained media of United’s form between his interim takeover in January and the end of last season.



Carrick declined to “dissect” United’s first loss since April as they suffered successive opening-day reverses in the Premier League era for the first time.

The United head coach stressed that although he appeared calm he was anything but inside yet would not “create chaos”.

He said: “I’m talking to you quite calm but I’m not exactly calm inside and enjoying the day. There’s a big difference.

“I’ve played here for a long time, you don’t get to play here for a long time without just going day by day, there are always ups and downs, and you just carry on as normal.

“It’s 100 per cent not that, it just doesn’t mean we have to shout and scream and create some chaos just because of it.



“Inside we’re hurting, the boys know we need to get better and the calmness doesn’t mean there’s no emotion in it.”

Sports.title: Bolt set to play Sunday league football for Manchester side
Sports.content:
Usain Bolt: From sprint stardom to Sunday league - athletics icon set for Wythenshawe Vets bow

Usain Bolt is registered to play for a Sunday league team in Manchester

Usain Bolt is registered to play for a Sunday league team in Manchester, with the Olympic champion set to make another foray into football.

The former sprint star, who still holds the world records for the 100m and 200m, has appeared on the squad list for Wythenshawe FC Veterans over-35s on the Football Association Full-Time website.

The team play in the Cheshire Veterans League, and feature a side made up of former top-level professionals.

Managed by former Manchester City and Republic of Ireland midfielder Stephen Ireland, the line-up also includes Danny Drinkwater, Antonio Valencia, Joleon Lescott, Emile Heskey, Marc Albrighton and Papiss Cisse.

Bolt, 40, is a major football fan, and has harboured an ambition to build a professional career in the sport since retiring following the World Championships in 2017.

Bolt still holds the world records for the 100m and 200m

His athletic career saw him win eight gold medals across three Olympics, and skyrocket to global fame.

The Jamaican became known for his trademark victory pose.

The star filed a patent application for the distinctive stance to market a range of products including sunglasses, jewellery, hats and sporting goods.

He briefly played for the Australian A-League team Central Coast Mariners.

The Manchester United supporter has also been a regular participant in Soccer Aid charity matches over the last decade.

He has also trained with other clubs across the world, most notably German heavyweights Borussia Dortmund.

Wythenshawe, yet to announce Bolt's signing, have been contacted for comment.

Sports.title: Everton outclass wasteful Palace in Premier League opener
Sports.content:
Everton made a winning start to the new Premier League campaign by beating Crystal Palace 2-0 thanks to classy goals from Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and Thierno Barry.

David Moyes's side ruthlessly punished their visitors, under the new charge of Frenchman Pierre Sage, for a series of missed opportunities, scoring either side of the break to register their first opening-weekend win for five years.

The performance was symptomatic of a team maturing under the influence of wily Moyes. The Everton boss entrusted 19-year-old Harrison Armstrong with a midfield role alongside new signing Hayden Hackney. Armstrong was involved in the first goal and Hackney connected to a superb second.

The teenager's hustle turned the ball over for Dewsbury-Hall to jinx inside Chris Richards and pick out the far corner just before half-time. Shortly after the break, Hackney's quick thinking from a free-kick got Iliman Ndiaye away and he picked out Barry with a cutting cross.

Image: Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall celebrates with Iliman Ndiaye after scoring Everton's opener

"Everton did a professional job. Armstrong and Hackney were very good," reflected Tim Sherwood on Soccer Saturday.

Palace, meanwhile, faded horribly after a promising opening. Their conversion issues appear to have been carried over from last season, with Jean-Philippe Mateta guilty of spurning a prime opportunity when the game was goalless, adding to the frustration of Eddie Nketiah's earlier miss. The former Arsenal forward drew a world-class save from Jordan Pickford but should have scored with a curling effort that was tipped onto the woodwork.

Palace's expected goals tally (2.04) was their highest in a Premier League game without scoring since December 2018.

Palace's openness suited Everton

Sky Sports' Tim Sherwood:

"I don't think there's any danger of Palace getting relegated or dragged into that sort of argument. They play a really attractive style of football but just sometimes you have to pick when to play open. They played right into the hands of Everton.

"Everton counter-attacked; they've got quality and pace on the counter and they've punished them.

"There's been some fantastic football played by Palace but they're on the wrong end of the result."

The key moments from Hill Dickinson Stadium

17: SAVE! Pickford denies Nketiah with a save-of-the-season contender, pushing his strike onto the frame of the goal.

38: POST! Nketiah picks out Mateta with a teasing low cross but the striker can only plant against the foot of the post.

43: GOAL! Dewsbury-Hall beats Dean Henderson with a sublime strike from a difficult angle.

53: GOAL! Barry rises highest to Ndiaye's clever cross and heads past Henderson.

68: SETBACK! Chadi Riad is stretchered off with a worrying knee injury.

Moyes praises midfield duo

Everton boss David Moyes:

"We could easily have been a couple of goals down. It was a worldie save [from Pickford to deny Nketiah]. It could have gone the other way.

"Once we got the first goal, it settled us. We managed the game well after that and contained Palace really well."

On the midfield duo: "They done great. Harrison is earning his place in the team, he's got an opportunity here, where at other clubs he might not have.

"With Hayden, sometimes boys from the Championship need time, but he's done well. I have to give him praise for how quickly he's picked things up."

Sports.title: Leicester booed off after nightmare defeat to Burton
Sports.content:
Burton Albion stunned Leicester City at the King Power Stadium, as the former Premier League champions were booed off after being beaten 2-1 by Gary Bowyer's side.

Matthew Dennis and Kgaogelo Chauke ensured Leicester's woeful start was punished before Russell Martin's men, who then saw Oliver Skipp receive a straight red card, finally showed some fight.

Only five minutes had passed when a move involving the excellent Charlie Webster ended with Kyran Lofthouse slipping the ball through to Dennis before he fired past Alex McCarthy. City fans were in uproar 20 minutes later after seeing Chauke react first when Lofthouse's shot was deflected into his path.

But when Skipp walked for a cynical foul on Curtis Tilt on the 29-minute mark, Wes Burn's first strike since joining from Ipswich - converting at the far post from Will Alves' cross - prevented the atmosphere from turning truly mutinous.

Harry Souttar headed over the bar and substitute Tommy Watson went close as City tried to mount a comeback.

Albion's defensive grit helped them overcome late pressure to claim a memorable victory.

Sports.title: 'The car is better for the race' - Hamilton 'optimistic' of Ferrari turnaround
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton believes his Ferrari car is in a "better place" after changes going into Dutch Grand Prix qualifying and that the team can still be "optimistic" for Sunday's race despite starting on the third row.

​​​​​​Ferrari are Mercedes' nearest challengers in both world championship races but qualified three tenths of a second away from pole at Zandvoort, F1's first event back after its summer break.

Fifth-fastest Hamilton and sixth-fastest Charles Leclerc will start behind both Mercedes and McLaren cars for a race that Lando Norris starts on pole position.

But fifth on the grid represented a step forward for Hamilton compared to the earlier Sprint sessions when he had qualified and finished seventh.

"Much different session, much different car," said Hamilton, who pipped Leclerc to the head of the third row with his final lap of Q3, to Sky Sports F1 after main qualifying.

"In Practice, the car felt great and was consistent but there are always areas you feel you can improve so we made subtle changes to try and fix those improvements and it flipped the car on its head and it was horrible through Sprint Qualifying and the Sprint. I had no confidence in the balance.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from qualifying for the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix.

"We made all these changes into Qualifying so I was learning a new car again, a new balance which I'm much happier with - trying to progress with it and learning with only like six laps was a challenge.

"Also all the Mercedes [powered cars] are ahead and we know we have a bit of a deficit on power so I think our race pace should be better and the car is better for the race."

Saturday's earlier Sprint race had appeared to prove that Ferrari's car was a competitive proposition around the twisty, undulating Zandvoort circuit.

Leclerc finished second, 1.3s behind winner George Russell, with his overtake on Norris with six laps to go the only change of position in the top 10 after the opening lap.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton had a nervous moment during Dutch GP qualifying where he found gravel just out of the first corner.

And despite the track not being especially friendly for overtaking, Hamilton is not ruling out the prospect of the SF-26 getting in the mix at the front again.

"I feel optimistic," he said.

"Fifth is not the greatest but it could be far worse, so I'm grateful to be there but of course I wish I was up further ahead.

"However, our race pace was good in the Sprint. Charles had good race pace and the car is in a better place

"Hopefully with the right strategy and right execution I think hopefully we can challenge the cars ahead."

What went wrong for Leclerc after Sprint promise?

Leclerc's overtake on Norris for second place with six laps to go in the Sprint had proved a relative surprise given he had been the only one of the front runners to run the 24-lap race on the soft tyres, a compound which is initially the fastest but on which performance falls away more quickly.

He had therefore been tipped to contend for pole but the Monegasque never ultimately appeared a contender in any of the three knockout sections.

"I don't think the conditions played a role," said Leclerc. "I think we changed the power strategies a bit too much throughout qualifying then in Q3 I had some weird things going on, so we lost a bit of performance there.

"At no time during qualifying [did I have] the potential of pole."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix Sprint race.

Dropped to sixth on Sunday's grid thanks to Hamilton's late improvement, Leclerc added on his race prospects: "Realistically it will be very difficult to overtake on track but we will do our best and see where we end up.

"Starting from sixth doesn't make our life easy, so it will be a tough race but the pace is there so I hope we can do something with strategy and offset ourselves to the others."

Team principal Frederic Vasseur, though, took heart from their Sprint performance and said the fact the race was likely to be a multi-stop affair could play in their favour.

"The race pace in the Sprint was very strong so we will try to come back," said the Frenchman.

"We had a good comparison between the two [tyre] compounds [in the Sprint] which is probably the best preparation we can have for the race.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Charles Leclerc overtakes Lando Norris in a 'beautiful' move to take second place.

"It's very difficult to overtake. It will probably be two or three pit stops which mean everything is open."

He also said the latest round of SF-26 upgrades, which include a new floor which was thought to be added to the car after the weekend's sole practice session on Friday, were performing as expected.

"It's working as per the plan," added Vasseur. "From the beginning of the season, every time we brought something it's worked per the plan.

"It's a positive side of the development this year. We are bringing a lot of upgrades at each race, not big ones, so we are not expecting to [gain] five tenths per race. But it's working as expected."

Sports.title: Carrick defends dismal Man Utd loss: 'It was never going to be perfect'
Sports.content:
Man Utd boss Michael Carrick focused on the "good things" his side had done despite a dismal 2-0 defeat at newly-promoted Hull City on the opening day of the new season.

United were outfought and outplayed by a Hull side widely tipped to return to the Sky Bet Championship this season at the MKM Stadium, with two goals from set pieces giving the Tigers a richly deserved victory and their first over United in more than half a century.

The loss punctured the optimism around Old Trafford at the start of Carrick's first full season in charge.

He had picked up more points than anyone else since returning to the club in January and had overseen the arrival of Andre Santos and Youri Tielemans - with Carlos Baleba likely to follow - before a shock defeat to a Hull side missing as many as eight first-team players brought things crashing back to earth.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Hull and Manchester United.

Despite losing 63 per cent of their duels and two thirds of their headers in a first half where Hull scored both their goals, Carrick said: "We did some good things today and it will get lost. We have to find answers but because we lose one game, it doesn't mean everything needs dissecting."

He added to TNT Sport: "Some of it was OK, there's bits to improve on. It was never going to be perfect, but going behind and giving ourselves a lot to do makes it more difficult.

"It was a typical one of those games, with a newly-promoted team at home. You can't give them much, they've got a lot to hold on to.

"After that, we had moments and opportunities but we didn't have the spark to put the chances away or create any more. We're bitterly disappointed with the result, but we won't let it knock us."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan gives us his three things to take away from Manchester United's loss to Hull City on the opening day of the season.

Captain Bruno Fernandes struck a more critical tone of his team-mates and said he had seen it all before as United were punished for their lack of aggression and intensity.

"It was the same mistakes we made last season, every away game we give too much of the ball to the opponent," he told TNT Sport.

"In the first 20 minutes, their goalkeeper was the one with the most touches.

"We needed to press more, be more aggressive, and then again we need to work on set-plays and not concede these type of goals.

"Against these types of teams, they are waiting for that moment. We knew before the game set-pieces would be a big part of their game."

Your views: Carrick already under pressure

Jay: "Carrick under pressure straight away. Eddie Howe anyone?"

Marek: "The job is too big for Carrick, he did a great job at the end of last season but Utd need a proven winner in charge."

Sports.title: Swansea & Sheff Utd play out dour draw
Sports.content:
Sheffield United put their latest financial worries to one side to earn a gritty draw against a toothless Swansea.

It was a second successive goalless scoreline for the Blades, who drew 0-0 at Birmingham last weekend.

Manager Chris Wilder and his team may have had their build-up distracted by the threat of a 12-point deduction for the club due to unpaid debts, but they looked focused and disciplined, if not very threatening.

They managed two shots on target, compared to a Sky Bet Championship low of zero last week, but that was one more than the Swans mustered.

The home side started with Adam Idah up front, sent on Zan Vipotnik, and ended up throwing on new signing Ross Stewart for his debut late on.

But all three failed to fire as Swansea were unable to make it successive wins at the start of the season following last week's victory at Stoke.

Despite the perfect conditions, neither side was able to display much quality in an error-strewn opening half hour.

Swansea applied most of the pressure and should have gone ahead when a floated corner from Josh Tymon in the 19th minute was allowed to bounce in the goalmouth, but none of his team-mates were able to take advantage.

Home winger Moussa Yeo then cut in from the left and was allowed two bites of the cherry to set up Elijah Just.

But the low grade stuff was summed up by the New Zealand World Cup star's total miskick from 12 yards out.

When the visitors did make a rare foray forward, midfielder Harrison Burrows was shown a yellow card for diving after what referee Tom Nield judged a fair tackle from Filip Lissah.

The Blades finally roused themselves in the late stages of the half and almost snatched the lead when Callum O'Hare's volley struck the underside of the bar.

Joe Rothwell's rebound effort was then charged down and Swansea managed to clear their lines.

Idah's strength opened up the Sheffield United defence early in the second half, but team-mate Joseph Opoku was unable to profit as his shot lacked power and direction.

The next opportunity spurned was down to the Blades' centre-back Mark McGuinness who sliced wide with a volley from a free-kick.

Swansea head coach Vitor Matos swapped Idah for last season's top scorer Vipotnik on the hour mark and followed that with a raft of other substitutions.

But the changes failed to lift the tempo for the home side and it was the Sheffield United striking pair of O'Hare and Patrick Bamford who looked the more threatening.

O'Hare cleverly got in behind Swansea's defence, but his cross was not anticipated by a teammate.

Swansea had a late surge but their finishing remained poor.

Sports.title: Fer Lopez scores twice in Wolves win
Sports.content:
Fer Lopez bagged a brace as Wolves secured their first victory of the Championship season with a convincing 3-1 success over Preston at Deepdale.

The Spaniard put Wanderers ahead with an eighth-minute rocket and substitute Adam Armstrong tucked home a 71st-minute second, just four minutes after stepping on to the pitch.

Lopez put a cherry on top of the cake with a poacher's finish in the 82nd minute as Cesar Peixoto's men really flexed their muscles, but substitute Jordan Thompson managed to bag a 25-yard consolation in the first minute of stoppage time to give the home faithful something to cheer.

It was a much-needed victory for the relegated Premier League side but Preston are now without a win in their opening two Championship matches.

A packed-out away end were on their feet from the off as Lopez ran in from the flank, virtually unchallenged from halfway having left Andrew Hughes for dead, before slamming past goalkeeper Daniel Iversen at his near post.

Wolves nearly doubled down on their rapid start twice in the opening 15 minutes as Marshall Munetsi dragged wide from a central position from just inside the box before Raul Jimenez back-flicked Jackson Tchatchoua's low delivery agonisingly wide of the far post.

Despite the setback, Ali McCann nearly rewarded a buoyant and lively home support with a shot from the edge of the box that deflected narrowly wide just shy of the half-hour and, from the resulting corner, Toti Gomes had to head Callum Lang's header off the line.

Preston did well to weather the early storm but needed Iversen to tip Rodrigo Gomes' low drive away as the Portuguese star wriggled into some space in first-half stoppage time.

Wolves began the second half how they started and indeed finished the first, with Iversen making a tremendous save to keep out Mateus Mane's first-time effort as he combined with Gomes.

Peixoto sent on Championship-proven goal-getter Armstrong in the 67th minute and the 29-year-old made his mark shortly afterwards as he coolly slotted beyond Iversen having played a one-two with Jimenez.

That seemed to be the straw that broke the camel's back as Lopez prodded in his second of the game following good work from Mane, whose teasing cross was flicked on by Tommy Doyle and turned in at the back post.

While Wolves were cruising to victory, there was still time for a moment of ingenuity as Thompson caught out Jose Sa with a well-placed shot from outside the box having been teed-up by Delano Burgzorg.

Sports.title: Castellanos misses late penalty as West Ham beaten by Charlton
Sports.content:
Charlton maintained their perfect start to the Championship season with a 2-1 victory at West Ham in a pulsating London derby to pile pressure on Hammers boss Nuno Espirito Santo.

Lloyd Jones and Tyreece Campbell put Charlton 2-0 ahead before Joel Piroe, signed on loan from Leeds, marked his first appearance for the east Londoners with a goal that set up a frantic finish.

Taty Castellanos then missed a stoppage-time penalty for the hosts that would have salvaged a point.

The Hammers handed debuts to Piroe and Arne Engels, but the pre-season promotion favourites were unable to force goalkeeper Arthur Okonkwo, put straight into the Charlton side after joining on a season-long loan from Wrexham on Thursday, into a strenuous save in the opening 45 minutes.

The south-east Londoners took the lead in the seventh minute. Sonny Carey's long throw was controlled on the chest by Jones with the Addicks captain producing an overhead finish past Mads Hermansen.

Winger Manor Solomon's goal-bound shot from the edge of the box was headed out for a corner by Addicks centre-back Billy Koumetio.

It could have got worse for West Ham with Miles Leaburn clipping the crossbar in the 19th minute. The counter was sparked by Campbell dispossessing Kyle Walkers-Peter.

Carey was then unable to beat Hermansen at the keeper's near post when the better option looked to be sliding Campbell in on the left of the penalty area.

West Ham striker Castellanos met Ollie Scarles' left-wing cross with a first-time header in first-half stoppage time but it was straight at Okonkwo.

Charlton doubled their advantage in the 56th minute. Konstantinos Mavropanos lost possession under pressure from Leaburn and Campbell finished clinically across Hermansen and into the bottom right corner of the net.

Okonkwo was finally called into serious action on the hour mark with a one-handed save to keep out Piroe's shot from the edge of the penalty area. Castellanos headed just wide of the post from another quality Scarles delivery.

West Ham ramped up the pressure and Piroe, who moments earlier had failed to convert a close-range header, slammed the ball home in the 74th minute after Okonkwo had initially parried a shot by Castellanos.

The Charlton keeper then produced a tremendous tip over to frustrate Hammers substitute Divine Mukasa, who joined on loan from Manchester City earlier this week.

Joe Rankin-Costello had the chance to add a third for the visitors but Hermansen was able to keep out the effort with his legs.

West Ham were given a lifeline in stoppage time when referee Andrew Kitchen penalised Conor Coventry for handball, but Castellanos' spot-kick hit the base of the right post.
