Sports.title: Burnham’s boys enjoy visit from Palace as Everton ease to opening day win
Sports.content:
Andy Burnham was in the posh seats at Hill Dickinson Stadium to witness how his beloved Everton would fare without the key additions to David Moyes’s team that even the Prime Minister had voiced an opinion on. No right-back, no new centre-forward, no problem: Everton capitalised on a wasteful Crystal Palace display to start their season with an ultimately convincing victory.

Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall swept any away lingering resentment over how last season ended for Everton with an outstanding finish before Thierno Barry, a man under pressure should a new striker arrive before the deadline, sealed the win with a second half header. It was a brutal introduction to the Premier League for the new Palace manager, Pierre Sage, who also lost the defender Chadi Riad to a potentially serious injury late on.

There were no radical changes in formation or personnel from Sage for his first Premier League outing. A lack of cutting edge was familiar from the Oliver Glasner era too. The visitors created three clear opportunities before Everton took the lead and failed to take any. Misfortune played its part in two of the chances, with Jordan Pickford’s left hand post struck twice, but that did not diminish the torment for Sage and the travelling support. A sense of the inevitable from Everton increased with each one.

View image in fullscreen Moved from his usual seat into the directors’ box by Prime Ministerial security logistics, Andy Burnham celebrated with the Everton legend, and his good friend, Peter Reid. Photograph: Paul Currie/Shutterstock

Palace denied reports before kick-off that Ismaïla Sarr had refused to play because of a desire to join Galatasaray – the Senegal international was absent due to injury, according to his new boss. – but the disruption had no impact on the visitors’ start. With three minutes gone, Everton’s new captain James Tarkowski misjudged a header and enabled Eddie Nketiah to break clear down the left. The forward picked out Jean-Philippe Mateta’s run to the near post but his strike partner volleyed over at close range.

Chance number two came from a sublime pass by Adam Wharton, the midfielder who Sage has insisted is going nowhere despite interest from Manchester City. Wharton found Nketiah free inside the area with a perfectly-weighted ball over Merlin Röhl, forced to deputise at right-back in the absence of a conclusion to Everton’s now farcical search for Seamus Coleman’s successor. Nketiah had time to pick his spot but Pickford produced a superb save to tip the shot onto his left hand post.

The same post was struck again when Wharton, the former Everton winger Dwight McNeil and Nketiah combined to find Mateta free in front of Pickford’s goal. At full stretch the France international beat Pickford only for the woodwork to rescue Everton once more. Moyes’s team took full advantage of their reprieves five minutes later.

View image in fullscreen Thierno Barry outjumped Chris Richards to head Everton into a two-goal lead just after half-time. Photograph: Peter Byrne/PA

Everton grew into their opening game, with summer signings Hayden Hackney, Tyrique George and Röhl all impressing. The hosts had an early chance of their own when Dewsbury-Hall released Röhl and the young German midfielder squared for Iliman Ndiaye to test Dean Henderson’s sharp reflexes in the Palace goal. Creativity was otherwise in short supply from the home side, despite George’s constant probing on the left, until Dewsbury-Hall and Ndiaye began to impose themselves on proceedings.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Dewsbury-Hall’s impact in particular was worth the wait. The midfielder burst into life with a mazy run that ended with an appeal for handball when his shot hit Chris Richards. Play continued through Daniel Muñoz, a potential Everton right-back target, who was dispossessed by the industrious Harrison Armstrong and left a void for Dewsbury-Hall to exploit. Receiving Armstrong’s pass, the 27-year-old swept an unstoppable, angled drive into Henderson’s far corner to open the season in style for Everton.

Muñoz should have made amends when stealing in ahead of George to meet an inviting delivery from Daichi Kamada. Palace’s end product did not match the build-up yet again, however, and the Colombian defender guided his header wide of the far post.

Everton found the comfort of a two-goal lead early in the second half when Ndiaye delivered a peach of a cross from the right. Barry, on a self-confessed mission to improve following a difficult debut season in the Premier League, rose between Richards and Jaydee Canvot to head past Henderson at close range. The departure of Riad on a stretcher, with the defender distraught as he was carried away, compounded Palace’s deflating afternoon.

Sports.title: Anton Stach snatches late Leeds winner to sour Glasner’s new dawn at Forest
Sports.content:
For Nottingham Forest, a few minutes before kick-off and before the curtain went up on another season, a new protagonist emerged from the tunnel. Oliver Glasner, Forest’s fifth head coach in less than 12 months, surveyed the scene from the home technical area. But the start of the new dawn, this Glasner’s first competitive game in the job, did not go to plan, Anton Stach sneaking a whipped free-kick in at Matz Sels’s near post with a couple of minutes of normal time remaining. At least Forest can put things right quickly, Leeds visiting in a Carabao Cup rematch on Tuesday.

Clearcut chances had been at a premium and Stach took matters into his own hands late on, after Nikola Milenkovic made a clumsy challenge on him on the edge of the penalty area. Sels got a glove on Stach’s effort but ended up wrapped around his right post, the Leeds support erupting with joy behind his goal.

Leeds were the more threatening side. In the first half, Harry Wilson had what would have been a debut goal disallowed when the assistant referee raised his flag for offside after the Welshman, whose arrival is evidence of Leeds’s ambition, latched on to Jayden Bogle’s pass into the box. In the second, Sels got a strong left hand to prevent another debutant, Tarik Muharemovic, a £34m buy from Sassuolo, from powering a header into the top corner.

Glasner, who named neither Ousmane Diomande, a £34m arrival from Sporting, nor Xaver Schlager in his starting lineup, puffed his cheeks as every outfield Leeds player joined the celebrations. At full time, the away end, bathed in the evening sun, was jubilant, the Forest areas had long since emptied.

View image in fullscreen Anton Stach jumps for joy after his late winner for Leeds. Photograph: Bruce Rollinson/PA

Leeds rationed Forest to moments in an underwhelming opener. Muharemovic had a fine debut alongside Joe Rodon and Jaka Bijol in their three-man defence. Glasner applauded when Neco Williams met Ola Aina’s cross from the right approaching the first-half interval. That chance led to Milenkovic and Jair Cunha combining to head against James Trafford’s post from James McAtee’s recycled cross but the Leeds goalkeeper was largely untroubled.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

These remain early days – Nuno Espírito Santo was in charge as Forest beat Brentford 3-1 in their opening game last season, with eight of the same starting XI – but Glasner’s side did little to enthuse the locals. More new faces are expected before the window closes next month. Chris Wood arrived from the bench and sent a bobbling Morgan Gibbs-White pass wide with a first-time shot. Schlager also entered for his debut but it was Leeds and Daniel Farke who were buoyed at the final whistle.

Sports.title: Ajayi and Mendy give Hull dream start against misfiring Manchester United
Sports.content:
Ever since Sir Alex Ferguson’s retirement 13 years ago, Manchester United have been stuck in football’s equivalent of purgatory and a chastening experience in Hull suggests they could be there a while longer. Michael Carrick’s permanent appointment was supposed to hail a new era at Old Trafford but very little has changed based on this defeat.

United were sluggish from start to finish and rightly punished for failing to defend set pieces with any degree of competence. Centre-backs Semi Ajayi and Nobel Mendy earned Hull the prized scalp upon their return to the Premier League while United are left to ponder if the squad requires more invasive surgery before the transfer window closes.

This was Hull’s first win against United in the Premier League while they had not beaten their rivals in 52 years. There had been a nine-year wait for the Tigers to be back at this level and they proved themselves worthy, admittedly against a toothless United, who lost their opening fixture for the fourth time in the past seven seasons.

Even with relatively little time on the clock, it felt like a game that needed a flashpoint to ignite the season. Harry Maguire and Elliot Stroud clashed around the halfway line, with both feeling wronged by the other, but nothing was given. The perceived injustice provoked the home players and supporters, increasing the level of intensity from Hull, while United retreated into their shell.

Warnings came as Senne Lammens saved from Oli McBurnie and tipped over a vicious Ryan Giles cross. Giles, however, delivered a corner that United failed to defend properly at either post. It was whipped to the front and flicked to the back where McBurnie had space to shoot. Lammens stopped it on the line, only for Ajayi to smash home only a second league goal for the club.

View image in fullscreen Semi Ajayi fires past Senne Lammens to put Hull ahead. Photograph: Paul Ellis/AFP/Getty Images

McBurnie was causing problems with his relentless running and physicality as Ayden Heaven was welcomed to the perils of Hull. United, on the other hand, missed the presence of a striker, with Matheus Cunha nominated for the role of a false No 9, which allowed him to roam far and wide, spending as much time away from Hull’s three centre-backs as possible.

United looked like a side playing their first game of pre-season against an opponent midway through the campaign. An avoidable free-kick given away by Youri Tielemans resulted in another set-piece United failed to deal with. Regan Slater’s delivery was dangerous and the lack of desire for anyone in white to attack the ball allowed Mendy to head a debut goal from close range. If this was supposed to be the start of a new United era, the reality was a return to the passive days of Ruben Amorim and his band of miserable men.

The Hull fans celebrated the half-time whistle with joy, while half the away end was empty, as souls searched for a way to soothe the pain on the concourse. It gave Carrick time to plot the radical change that was required but he only removed the cautioned Patrick Dorgu, sending on the returning Marcus Rashford.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Nobel Mendy (left) sparks wild celebrations for Hull in their first league win against Manchester United since 1974. Photograph: George Wood/Getty Images

Carrick brought calm after replacing Amorim but playing with this much tranquility was naive. Tactics and natural ability need to be blended with fight and desire, traits not on display from United, who would have hoped for a promising start, especially with Ipswich at home next.

Rashford was introduced to provide the previously absent spark and make the team less narrow and more expansive. He brought something akin to intent on the left wing, running at defenders who had walked through the first half but nothing was created as Konstantinos Tzolakis enjoyed a comfortable debut. It was a sign of how the day had gone for United when debutants Andrey Santos and Tielemans, signed for a combined total of £85m, were withdrawn with 23 minutes remaining after struggling to get a foothold in the game.

Hull, who had the fourth worst defensive record in the Championship last season, did not need to attack in the second half and were happy to keep United at arm’s length. The hosts deserved everything they received, through a mixture of quality delivery, aggression and organisation, three things United lacked. Football, bloody Hull.

Sports.title: Jack Clarke’s last-minute strike secures Ipswich winning return against Sunderland
Sports.content:
It would be fascinating to know what recruitment algorithms or eagle-eyed staff in Ipswich’s recruitment department spotted the potential and capability in Emersonn to score the goals to keep them in the Premier League. Thirteen games, no goals and a serious knee injury at the Brazilian side Athletico Paranaense, two league goals in 17 games at the Turkish side Goztepe, then six in 28 at the French side Toulouse. A modest return, for sure, but it doesn’t scream ready to break down doors in the English top flight.

Ipswich have spent more than £150m this summer, intent on not making the same mistakes as the last time they came up, which detailed analysis presumably showed was not spending enough money. Emersonn became a club record signing, at £24m plus add-ons, beaten a month later by the arrival of the attacking midfielder Julio Enciso, for £26m.

In a season of flux and uncertainty, the sparks of a compelling partnership between the pair in the opening weekend win against Sunderland offered the faintest hope that Ipswich can defy the odds and stay up this season.

They combined for the opening goal, one that started with a gift from Sunderland but turned into an impressive display of skill and precision.

Luke O’Nien, for reasons unbeknownst to anyone but Luke O’Nien, had the ball under no pressure on halfway but passed straight to Enciso. Anyone watching the previous 23 minutes could tell the quick-footed, tricky No 10 was the last person you wanted to give the ball to with yards of open grass behind you.

Enciso duly skipped past O’Nien and drove into Sunderland’s half, then when Dan Ballard came across to cover shimmied past him, too. It was then a simple pass across, bypassing the onrushing goalkeeper, Robin Roefs, for Emersonn to tuck the ball away scruffily.

There is indubitable flair and talent in the 22-year-old – the first Brazilian to play for Ipswich. A little later, with the ball on the left, he evaded Thomas Meunier and Enzo Le Fée by slipping the ball between them, then found Enciso with a low cross, but the attacking midfielder caught the ball wrong and it flew over.

View image in fullscreen Emersonn celebrates scoring Ipswich’s first goal against Sunderland. Photograph: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images

Enciso has returned to Ipswich as though intent on making up for lost time. He’s had nibbles at the Premier League before – first at Brighton, where he couldn’t quite move beyond useful-player-to-bring-on, before a loan to Ipswich the last time they were here, where he did well but they ultimately went down.

There will be times in retirement when O’Nien will wake up, drenched in sweat, from feverish dreams replaying over and over what Enciso did to him on this afternoon. On another occasion, Enciso darted in to steal the ball from O’Nien’s feet, the defender taking a yellow card to avoid being humiliated again.

And if it wasn’t O’Nien, it was others. In another flowing move, Enciso chopped easily passed Granit Xhaka – the midfielder, unused to being beaten like that, shaking his head in frustration – then cut inside Nilson Angulo and crossed to the back post, where Emersonn was unable to head on target.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Enciso has the vibe of a diminutive forward who will have a worldy performance once every four or five games – just enough that you think if he could only find that consistency, he would be one of the best players in the league. Rather than at Ipswich. Perhaps he will prove that prediction wrong: his deft flick on the turn, attempting to turn Abdul Fatawu’s driven in-swinging ball inside the far post, but missing by inches, was evidence of a football brain few share.

For most of the second half it appeared as though all their good work would not deliver three points. Six minutes before half-time, Sunderland won a free-kick on the edge of Ipswich’s penalty area – a fraction off to the left – and Angulo swept the ball in marvellously via the crossbar.

But Jack Clarke came on in the 71st minute – replacing Enciso, the man of the match leaving to a standing ovation – and in the 90th minute he dribbled towards backing-off defenders and delicately finished into the bottom right corner.

Ipswich are back – and there is something different about them.

Sports.title: Championship roundup: Nuno feels the heat after West Ham beaten by Charlton
Sports.content:
Charlton maintained their perfect start to the Championship season with a 2-1 victory at West Ham in a pulsating London derby to pile more pressure on the Hammers manager Nuno Espírito Santo.

Lloyd Jones and Tyreece Campbell put Charlton 2-0 ahead before Joel Piroe, signed on loan from Leeds, marked his first appearance for the east Londoners with a goal that set up a frantic finish. Taty Castellanos then missed a stoppage-time penalty for the hosts that would have salvaged a point.

Fer López bagged a brace as Wolves secured their first victory of the season with a convincing 3-1 success over Preston at Deepdale. The Spaniard put Wanderers ahead with an eighth-minute rocket and substitute Adam Armstrong tucked home a 71st-minute second, just four minutes after stepping on to the pitch.

View image in fullscreen Fer López scores Wolves’s third of the match to kill off Preston. Photograph: Gary Oakley/PA

López put a cherry on top of the cake with a poacher’s finish in the 82nd minute as Cesar Peixoto’s men lexed their muscles, but substitute Jordan Thompson managed to bag a 25-yard consolation in the first minute of stoppage time to give the home faithful something to cheer.

It was a much-needed victory for the relegated Premier League side but Preston are now without a win in their opening two Championship matches.

Blackburn stunned Middlesbrough with two goals in the space of six second-half minutes to earn a 2-1 victory at Ewood Park which continues their impressive start to the season. After conceding late against Wolves, the early signs pointed to more misery for Rovers as Kim Hellberg’s side smothered them early and were rewarded through Jeremy Sarmiento’s composed 12th-minute finish.

Rovers created enough in that first half to give their fans encouragement and pounced after the break through Andri Gudjohnsen’s 49th-minute header – his second goal in as many games – and Todd Cantwell’s diving header six minutes later to complete the turnaround.

Divin Mubama scored a dramatic late goal on his home debut to help Southampton to a 3-1 victory over his former club Stoke. Almost a year ago, the Manchester City loan striker was sent off for Stoke at St Mary’s for diving.

Here, he was the hero as Saints dug deep to preserve an unbeaten home run which stretches back to January. Ryan Manning also scored a stoppage-time penalty after Svante Ingelsson was sent off for bringing down Samuel Edozie.

Cyle Larin bagged his third goal in as many games to give Tonda Eckert’s side an early lead but Stoke hit back through Ethan Galbraith and looked good value for a point until late on.

Wrexham were kept waiting for their first Championship win of the season as they drew 1-1 with Watford in front of Hollywood owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac.

Both goals at the Racecourse Ground came in the opening quarter with Luca Kjerrumgaard’s header cancelled out by Danny Imray’s first Wrexham goal. It meant another draw for Wrexham after the Red Dragons were denied by a last-gasp Cardiff equaliser on Monday.

View image in fullscreen Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac watch Wrexham draw 1-1 with Watford. Photograph: Ryan Browne/Shutterstock

Cardiff remain unbeaten two games into their return to second-tier football after Cian Ashford and Yousef Salech’s goals earned a 2-2 draw at Derby.

The Bluebirds were good value for their point, having twice taken the lead in front of a raucous Pride Park crowd of 28,926.

But the Rams, unconvincing for large periods, capitalised on defensive mishaps to earn their first point of the new campaign through Carlton Morris and Bobby Clark.

Tairyk Arconte scored his first two goals for Millwall as they breezed past 10-man Norwich 3-0 to make it two wins from two this season. Having been tipped to challenge for the playoffs, Norwich have lost both of their opening games and had defender José Córdoba sent off in the second half at The Den.

Millwall were rewarded for their lively start in the 18th minute when Mark Sykes’s ball found Josh Coburn, whose shot was pushed out by Vladan Kovacevic for Arconte to tap in the rebound on his home debut.

Millwall deservedly went 2-0 ahead after 58 minutes when Zak Sturge’s ball into the box was headed back by Jake Cooper for Arconte to steer a volley into the bottom corner.

Norwich’s afternoon went from bad to worse in the 64th minute when Córdoba was sent off for a second yellow card after bundling over Arconte as he charged towards the area.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Victory was sealed with six minutes remaining when a slick counterattack ended with Luke Cundle sliding in Millwall’s third.

View image in fullscreen Tairyk Arconte celebrates scoring Millwall’s second goal of the game against Norwich City. Photograph: George Tewkesbury/Shutterstock

Alex Neil, the Millwall manager, said: “I thought it was a complete performance from us, probably the most complete performance we’ve had in the nearly 20 months I’ve been here. We were the best team from minute one to the last minute.”

Philippe Clement, whose side have lost their first two league games, said: “In the first half we were bullied. We didn’t win duels, second balls. When they pressed us, we were not brave enough on the ball.”

Portsmouth claimed their first win of the season with a comprehensive 3-1 success at Lincoln. Portsmouth, who had lost their first two games of the campaign by the same scoreline, found themselves under the cosh early on, but a seventh-minute goal from Ryan Kavuma-McQueen put them in the driving seat.

Adrian Segecic doubled the lead nine minutes later before Reeco Hackett-Fairchild pulled one back from the spot just past the half-hour mark.

Substitute Ebrima Adams made the game safe with a superb strike after 69 minutes to leave Lincoln still searching for their first win back in the second tier for more than 60 years.

The Pompey manager, John Mousinho, said: “There were two aspects I was pleased with – we stood up to Lincoln’s physical threat pretty well for the most part and then when we settled down and played, we broke through the lines well and had a real attacking threat.”

The Lincoln joint head coach Tom Shaw was disappointed with the result on such a big day for the club. “After a good start, the first goal knocked the wind out of our sails. I was pleased with how we responded, but the second half just petered out a bit.”

Demarai Gray rescued a point for Birmingham with a late penalty in a 2-2 draw at home to Bristol City. Scott Twine’s 33rd-minute effort gave the visitors the advantage before they conceded a 42nd-minute equaliser to Carlos Vicente. Dom Ballard converted Rio Cardines’s cross with a superb flick with his back to goal after 85 minutes to restore Bristol City’s lead but they could not hold on.

Jhon Solis had an 88th-minute equaliser ruled out for offside and the Birmingham manager, Chris Davies, said: “I was furious and in disbelief to have that goal disallowed for some involvement on the goalkeeper. I just don’t see it and I don’t think they even appealed for it.”

QPR’s Richard Kone missed several chances in a goalless draw with Bolton at Loftus Road. Kone, left out for last weekend’s win at Portsmouth, was restored to the Rangers side but missed four clear-cut opportunities during a first half largely dominated by the hosts.

Callum O’Hare came closest to netting a winner but Sheffield United had to be content with a goalless draw at Swansea City.

Sports.title: ‘See you at the hairdresser’s’: Gianni Infantino’s bizarre reply to bald reporter
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino told a reporter “I’ll see you at the hairdresser’s” after he was asked whether he had betrayed football over his aborted World Cup sell-off plan.

The Fifa president was stopped outside a hotel in the Dominican Republic by the Sky News US correspondent, James Matthews, who challenged the under-fire leader of football’s governing body over why he had not resigned, despite calls from across the game for him to step down.

Last week, three continental confederations accused the president of “deception” over his plans to secure private investment in Fifa tournaments, while the European governing body Uefa has threatened a boycott of Fifa competitions having “lost confidence” in his leadership.

Having tracked Infantino to a hotel in the Caribbean country where he has travelled to attend a youth tournament, Matthews, who shares Infantino’s recognisable bald pate, asked the 56-year-old whether he had “betrayed the game of football”, to which came the reply: “You have a nice haircut. Thank you so much”.

As the president walked away, Matthews continued: “Why won’t you resign? Fans, Fifa associations want you to step down. Why won’t you? Have you betrayed the trust of Fifa?”

As he stepped inside a waiting black car, Infantino replied: “I’ll see you at the hairdresser’s.”

Infantino has defied a request by one of his Fifa vice presidents to stay away from the under-14 tournament in the Caribbean and instead made a rare public appearance during the global furore over his failed plan to sell future World Cup profits to private investors.

On Saturday, Infantino posted photos on his Instagram account of him meeting political and football officials from the Dominican Republic on the sidelines of a Caribbean Football Union (CFU) youth tournament in the Punta Cana resort.

Infantino had been asked not to attend by Victor Montagliani, the Canadian president of Miami-based Concacaf to avoid being a distraction from the event. “I believe that considering the governance crisis surrounding Fifa as a result of your controversial FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal, the media will focus on this situation which will unfortunately significantly take away from the technical nature of the CFU youth competition,” Montagliani wrote in an email seen by Associated Press. “As such, I respectfully ask you in the name of football to reconsider your attendance as it will unfortunately undermine the technical nature of this important youth development activity.”

Fifa declined to comment on the Montagliani request, though noted it directly funds regional bodies like the CFU with up to $5m from each four-year World Cup cycle.

Caribbean member federations are seen as potential supporters for Infantino to peel away from their Concacaf leadership. South America’s Conmebol has backed Infantino as its best path to hosting more games at the 2030 World Cup it wants expanded from 48 teams to 64.

Infantino is aiming to be re-elected for a fourth and final term in office through to 2031 at the Fifa election congress in March in Morocco.

Sports.title: Andy Burnham says he wants to bring men’s World Cup back to UK in 2042
Sports.content:
Andy Burnham has said he wants to bring the men’s World Cup to the UK in 2042, returning the tournament to Britain for the first time in almost eight decades.

During informal discussions at No 10 North in Manchester on Friday, the prime minister told regional mayors he was keen for the tournament to be played in the British Isles.

The World Cup took place in England in 1966, when the home side beat West Germany 4-2 in the final after extra time – the only time the country has either hosted or won the contest.

Burnham, a keen football fan who has a season ticket at Everton, said earlier this month that it was “insane” only one World Cup had been held anywhere in the UK.

It is understood an application to stage the competition could also involve other home nations, none of which have hosted any World Cup games.

In recent years, joint bids between countries for major football tournaments have become more common. Alongside the Republic of Ireland, England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland will host the men’s European championships in 2028.

Work has not yet begun on any official bid for the 2042 event but it is understood Downing Street would support the FA should it choose to pursue it.

Sources say Burnham has “broad aspirations” and “a general ambition” to bring more major footballing events to the UK.

England made a doomed bid to host the 2018 World Cup, which was awarded to Russia amid allegations of corruption.

In 2014, while serving in the shadow cabinet, Burnham said he was uncomfortable that the tournament was still allowed to take place in Russia after its annexation of Crimea.

Under Fifa regulations, no European country would be eligible to stage the World Cup until 2042.

In 2000, Fifa introduced rules that meant the tournament would be rotated around its six continental confederations. It led to South Africa hosting its first World Cup in 2010, but the strict system was scrapped in October 2007.

Countries are not allowed to bid to stage a World Cup if either of the previous two tournaments have taken place on the same continent.

The 2030 World Cup will be hosted by Spain, Portugal and Morocco, with some early matches taking place in South America to mark the tournament’s centenary. The first World Cup was played in Uruguay in 1930.

Fifa has also confirmed that the 2034 tournament will take place in Saudi Arabia. The location of the 2038 World Cup has not yet been announced, but under the rules, it is likely to be played in North America or Oceania, which includes Australia and New Zealand.

Burnham is also understood to have spoken about the possibility of hosting the Olympic and Paralympic Games in the north of England in the 2040s at Friday’s meeting.

UK Sport was commissioned to assess whether a bid would be viable earlier this year under the previous prime minister, Keir Starmer.

It is understood that the government is considering the possibility of a “multi-city bid” in an attempt to spread any economic benefit between several northern cities.

A government spokesperson said: “The UK is committed to delivering world-class major sporting events with pride, with the Tour de France and Tour de France Femmes Grands Départs 2027 and Uefa Euro 2028 secured, and active bids for the 2029 World Athletics Championships and 2035 Women’s World Cup.



“As the prime minister has made clear, we will continue to pursue sporting events that bring communities together, drive regional growth and create jobs across the country.”

Sports.title: ‘Absolutely pathetic’ – EFL club told to have emergency board meeting and sack manager
Sports.content:
Adrian Durham has urged Norwich to sack manager Philippe Clement after his 'pathetic' rant about VAR before his side's defeat to Millwall.

The Belgian's nightmare start to the season continued on Saturday, as the Canaries fell to a demoralising 3-0 loss at the Den.



3 Philippe Clement's Norwich have no points on the board after their first two Championship games Credit: Getty

A Tairyk Arconte double before Luke Cundle's late goal made it two defeats from two for Norwich this campaign, who were reduced to ten men after Jose Cordoba was dismissed in the second half.

This leaves Clement's side 23rd in the Championship already, with only Southampton below them thanks to their four-point deduction.

Norwich's drubbing at the hands of Millwall came just a week after their opening-day defeat to Blackburn was marred by controversy.



The Baggies ran out 2-1 winners at Carrow Road, but were handed a slice of good fortune when Aune Heggebo's opener came via him diverting the ball into the net with his hand.

Despite the appeals of the Norwich players, the goal was allowed to stand by referee Tim Robinson.



The goal quickly went viral on social media, leading to calls for VAR to be introduced, while Heggebo was later handed a two-game ban by the EFL for ‘successful deception of a match official’.

What did Clement say about VAR?

A day before Norwich's clash with Millwall, Clement delivered a passionate rant calling for VAR to be introduced to the Championship, naming all 71 countries that use the technology.



In a seven-minute long monologue, the ex-Rangers boss said: “I think the league creates its own problems by not having VAR.

“I didn’t want to go into that after the game because you want to focus on the team and the things we could do better, and clearly there are things the referees could have done better.

“But I know it’s real time it goes fast, and there are errors made by human beings.

3 Tairyk Arconte's double saw Millwall put Norwich to the sword on Saturday Credit: Getty



“That’s why there’s VAR. So the next morning, you’re still gutted about things, and then I asked my analyst to look up, in which leagues around the world, there is VAR.

"So that’s why I have this list.”

Clement then stopped the press conference to read out all 71 countries that use VAR, even taking time to specify which nations have it across more than one division – unlike England.

He added: “So all these leagues have VAR. There are countries that never played in a World Cup here.

“It’s madness for me that there’s no VAR in the Championship.”

What has Adrian Durham said about Clement?

Less than 24 hours on from Clement's VAR plea, his rant backfired as Norwich were well beaten at the Den, and talkSPORT's Durham was less than impressed with their manager's behaviour.



3 Norwich have now shipped in five goals from their opening two Championship games Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Reacting to the result on air, Durham said: "Millwall 3-0 Norwich City was the full-time score.

“Millwall looked really good when I was watching them last week at Bristol City and they backed it up with a big home win against Norwich who had Jose Cordoba sent off at.

Delivering a scathing verdict on Clement, Durham then fumed: “Any wonder Norwich were battered at Millwall.



“Philippe Clement the manager told his analysts to find out all the countries that have VAR instead of using his analysts to find out about his opponents Millwall.

“Absolutely pathetic rant about VAR - should have led to an emergency board meeting at Norwich and he should no longer be the manager, but that's just my opinion.“

Clement took over at Norwich in November 2025, nine months on from his sacking by Rangers, and guided his side to a ninth-place finish last term.

And while the Canaries were tipped for a play-off push before the season began, their manager's main focus now will be getting some points on the board as they look to get out of the Championship relegation zone.

Sports.title: Hull fans send clear message to Joe Cole during upset win over Man United as manager hits back
Sports.content:
Hull fans send clear message to Joe Cole during upset win over Man United as manager hits back

Hull City fans have had the first laugh and are hoping they have the last one too.

The Tigers announced their return to the Premier League with a superb 2-0 win over Manchester United in the lunchtime kick off.

4 Nobel Mendy's header fired Hull into a deserved 2-0 lead shortly before half time Credit: Getty

4 Hull fans were delirious after their side's perfect start to the season Credit: AFP

First-half goals from Semi Ajayi and Nobel Mendy were enough to see off Michael Carrick’s men at the MKM Stadium and claim three valuable points in the club’s quest for survival.

And there was a little bit of history made as Sergej Jakirovic became the first Hull manager to beat Manchester United in the Premier League.

But attention from the stands quickly turned to TNT Sports pundit Joe Cole after comments he made about the club’s chances of survival earlier this week alongside our very own Carlton Cole, who refused to apologise on last night's Sports Bar Weekender.

Former Chelsea and West Ham midfielder Joe Cole revealed that he intentionally ignored a request from TNT Sports to cover Hull’s Premier League opener.

Speaking on the 'Dressing Room' podcast alongside Carlton Cole, he also predicted that the club are certain to be relegated at the end of the season.

And it’s fair to say that his comments did not go down well with the Premier League new boys.

That led to Hull owner Acun Ilicali publicly slamming Cole’s comments live on talkSPORT on Friday.

And that was backed up by a packed out MKM Stadium on Saturday who called out the pundit during the match.

Fans were heard chanting: “Are you watching Joe Cole?"

The chants took place as Hull fans revelled in their side’s brilliant performance to sweep aside Carrick’s expensively-assembled side.

4 TNT Sports pundit Joe Cole came under fire this week for his comments on Hull Credit: Getty

Hull will use their detractors as a source of motivation

After the match, Jakirovic also had his say on Cole’s comments and his side’s objectives for the season.

“It’s a big motivation for us because somebody underestimated you, especially from an ex-player,” Jakirovic told talkSPORT.

“Because you were a professional and know how difficult it is to get promotion from the Championship to the Premier League. It’s not easy.

“This is a big motivation for us and we will try to prove all these people wrong. This is our main goal this season.”

Cole did receive support over his comments from namesake and former teammate Carlton Cole.

The ex-Premier League striker took to Instagram urging fans not to take Cole's comments too seriously and passed it off as 'banter'.

4 Sergej Jakirovic says he will use Cole's comments to rally his troops this season Credit: Getty

"We've come under a bit of fire at the Dressing Room. The Hull City fans are not happy with us,"

"Listen, a bit of back and forth, a bit of banter, it's alright. It's not the end of the world. One man's opinion doesn't make it right, doesn't make it real.

"You might be disappointed with that opinion, but it's alright. That's the whole point of football. Yes, I did belly laugh when he said that you snuck in at the back door. I did. Come on, it's funny. I'm laughing at my mate's joke. I can do that.

"Joe thinks that you won't stay up and it's alright if you don't stay up. It's okay. You've done well to get to this point.

"I love Hull City," he continued. "I've got admiration for Hull City. My son was there. He's now at Middlesbrough, but when I look back, the fans were amazing.

He added: "So what I want from you is to suggest a forfeit. If you do stay up, or anybody that thinks Hull's going to stay up, send your suggestions in for a forfeit for Joe Cole."

With three points on the board, Hull quickly turn their attention to the Carabao Cup and a midweek trip to Championship side Stoke City.

Then it is back to Premier League duty with a trip to fellow promoted club Coventry before clashes against Aston Villa, Chelsea and Newcastle.

Sports.title: Premier League club set to sign Leon Goretzka on free transfer after Bayern Munich exit
Sports.content:
Premier League club set to sign Leon Goretzka on free transfer after Bayern Munich exit

Aston Villa are closing in on the signing of Leon Goretzka, talkSPORT understands.

The midfielder is a free agent having left Bayern Munich earlier this summer after eight seasons, where he won seven Bundesliga titles.

2 Goretzka is on his way to the Premier League to join Europa League holders Villa Credit: Getty

In total he has featured 327 times in the German top-flight, while also playing in 73 games in the Champions League.

And Villa will be hoping that European experience helps them with the club preparing for their second European Cup campaign in the last three seasons.

Goretzka is also highly experienced at international level having been capped on 73 occasions for the German national team.

And having spent his entire career in Germany, he is now set to test himself in the Premier League with Villa.

The Midlands outfit have turned to the 31-year-old after missing out on his ex-Bayern teammate Joao Palhinha, who spent last season on loan at Tottenham Hotspur.

Palhinha ultimately opted to reunite with his ex-Fulham boss Marco Silva in Portugal at Benfica.

And Villa have acted fast in looking to secure Goretzka's services in what is a major boost to Unai Emery.

He is now set to undergo his Villa medical next week after reaching a verbal agreement with the Europa League holders.

If all goes to plan, he could make his debut against Premier League champions Arsenal on Monday, August 31.

Who have Villa signed this summer ?

Emery has made strengthening his midfield a top priority this window, with Amadou Onana suffering an ACL injury whilst playing for Belgium at the World Cup.

2 Emery has been looking to bolster his midfield this summer Credit: Getty

Youri Tielemans then departed Villa a few days later to Manchester United, so it came as no surprise that they entered the market for midfielders.

Johan Manzambi was signed from SC Freiburg for £52million, and then Joao Gomes was brought in from rivals Wolves in a £38m move.

Elsewhere, left-back Matteo Ruggeri and goalkeeper Zion Suzuki have also joined a dismantled Villa side.

Though key players Morgan Rogers, Lucas Digne and Ezri Konsa have followed Tielemans out the exit this summer.

Ollie Watkins could also leave before the window slams shut as he wants to join Al Hilal in the Saudi Pro League.

Chelsea forward Nicolas Jackson, a long-term target for Villa and ex-player of Unai Emery at Villarreal, could replace him.

Villa are also interested in Southampton centre-back Taylor Harwood-Bellis as they prepare for their Premier League opener away at Brighton on Sunday.

Sports.title: Ex-Championship player Quevin Castro dies aged 25 after collapsing in friendly
Sports.content:
Former West Brom player Quevin Castro has tragically died at the age of 25.

Castro collapsed during a training match while playing for third-tier Portuguese side Real Sport Clube (Massama) on Saturday.

2 Castro spent two years at West Brom between 2021 and 2023 Credit: Getty

Primeira Liga club Estrela da Amadora hosted the friendly in Malveira and Castro was taken ill in the tenth minute.

A club doctor made attempts to revive the player with a defibrillator and the INEM (National Institute of Medical Emergency) was called.

The Portuguese midfielder was taken to hospital and pronounced dead shortly after arrival.

Estrela de Amadora expressed their condolences in an official statement on their website.

The club said: "Estrela da Amadora hereby expresses its deepest condolences for the passing of Quévin Castro, a player for Real Massamá.

"At this moment of profound sadness, Estrela da Amadora extends its deepest condolences to the family and friends of Quévin Castro, as well as to the entire Real Massamá structure.

"Our thoughts are with all those who were close to him.

"Rest in peace, Quévin."

His former club, Isthmian League Premier side Eastbourne Borough, paid tribute on social media.

The club said: "EBFC are devastated to learn of the passing of former player Quevin Castro.

2 Castro played for numerous clubs in England Credit: Getty

"Our thoughts are with Quevin's family during this extremely difficult time.

"Rest in Peace, Quevin."

Castro was most recently at the seventh-tier English side before returning to his homeland earlier this summer.

Having been born in Portugal, he grew up in Norfolk and went to school at Thetford Academy.

He also played for West Brom, Burton, Notts County, York City and Cambridge City during his time in English football.

Castro also spent time on trial with Arsenal and Chelsea.

Sports.title: Man United make last-minute Marcus Rashford announcement after programme confusion
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford was given Manchester United's No.9 shirt after being listed without a squad number on the matchday programme for the trip to Hull.

But the 28-year-old was unable to inspire his side to victory after coming off the bench in the Red Devils' shock 2-0 defeat at the MKM Stadium on Saturday.



2 Rashford was brought on for the start of the second half with the Tigers 2-0 up Credit: Getty

Returning to the United set-up following his season-long loan at Barcelona, Rashford was named amongst the substitutes for the clash in Yorkshire.

And it was the forward who boss Michael Carrick turned to at half-time with his side trailing two goals at the break.

Having seen his No.10 jersey given to Matheus Cunha last summer, the England international was bizarrely the only Manchester United player listed without a number on the match programme’s squad list.



The mishap appears to show that the final say on Rashford’s shirt number was a late decision that was taken after the programme went to print.

And while he wore the No.9 shirt in last weekend's pre-season defeat to AC Milan, it had been thought he would take the vacant No.14 - the number he wore during his time in Catalonia.



What number will Marcus Rashford wear for Man United this season?

But just two hours before their season-opening loss, the club finally announced its official list of squad numbers for the upcoming campaign, confirming that Rashford will don the No.9 shirt.

The former Aston Villa loan star then came on for the second half in what was his first competitive outing for United since December 2024.



And while his introduction ultimately failed to spark a comeback for the visitors, he was their brightest spark in what was a disastrous day for United.

In what was a truly nightmare day for supporters, who were already facing a bleak journey home, an announcement over the tannoy at the MKK Stadium informed them that the 15.03 and 17.03 trains back to Manchester had been cancelled.

Speaking to talkSPORT's Sam Matterface following the shock loss, Carrick was asked whether Rashford will remain at the Theatre of Dreams beyond the window.

2 Rashford's squad number was confirmed just two hours before kick-off Credit: Getty



United fans are already urging for Rashford to make a return to the line-up when Ipswich Town travel to Old Trafford next weekend.

And Carrick has declared he is 'delighted' to once again count on Rashford, as he played down the importance of him wearing the No.9.

Will Rashford be staying at United after transfer deadline day?

Carrick said: "He came on today and he done everything he could to try and make a difference for us,.

"Just because he's got the No.9, it doesn't really have a massive impact on whatever, he's got to wear some number.



"So we've been delighted to have him and he was trying things down the side with Luke [Shaw] today.

"Just couldn't quite find that moment for us, but, as I said, we're delighted to have him."

Sports.title: Russell Martin’s Leicester tenure threatens to turn toxic with shock home league defeat
Sports.content:
Leicester City have continued their worrying start to the season with a dismal defeat against Burton Albion.

The Foxes, who were crowned Premier League champions ten years ago, remain winless in League One and conceded after five minutes.

2 Leicester have made a torrid start to life in League One Credit: Getty

Matthew Dennis was on hand to put Burton ahead at the King Power Stadium from inside the area to leave the hosts stunned.

A defensive mess then led to Kegs Chauke netting the second, before Oliver Skipp was sent off to send Leicester down to ten men.

Leicester fans made their feelings known with boos, and some even chanted 'You're not fit to wear the shirt'.

Wes Burns managed to pull one back on the stroke of half-time to salvage some pride in what was otherwise a shocking first-half.

But they failed to equalise during the second and have therefore just picked up one point from a possible six, with boos ringing out once again at the full-time whistle.

Russell Martin will already be under pressure as manager, just weeks after taking the job, following the defeat.

He won his first match in charge with a 1-0 victory over Northampton in the Carabao Cup first round.

However, they had to settle for a 1-1 draw at Notts County in their league opener after a poor defensive showing led to a late equaliser.

Defeat against Burton only adds to the uncertainty over the future of the club.

Leicester owners King Power have recently put them up for sale, and are expected to bank in excess of £200million.

2 Martin will need to quickly win over the Leicester fans Credit: Getty

Scottish-Indian businessman Neil Lal has announced that he is eyeing a potential purchase via a consortium.

Back on the pitch, Leicester will be desperate to secure promotion back to the Championship at the first time of asking.

However, as it stands, they are potentially on course for what would be an unprecedented battle against relegation to League Two.

Their latest result puts them 18th in the table and just one point off the bottom four on goal difference.

Sports.title: EFL clash suspended for eight minutes as player hospitalised in sickening incident
Sports.content:
EFL clash suspended for eight minutes as player hospitalised in sickening incident

Luton Town’s League One match against Notts County was suspended for eight minutes after a horrifying clash of heads.

The Saturday lunchtime fixture at Kenilworth Road was marred by the incident that occurred just nine minutes into the match.



2 Luton's Jordan Clark was stretchered off after the clash of heads Credit: Getty

Luton midfielder Jordan Clark and Notts County’s Darius Lipsiuc both attempted to head a cross from Emilio Lawrence.

But the collision that followed caused widespread concern.

Both sets of players quickly attended to Clark who appeared to come off worse from the clash.

Paramedics quickly arrived on the scene to treat the 32-year-old before he was lifted onto a stretcher and carried off the pitch.



Notts County goalkeeper James Belshaw somehow managed to keep the attempt out of his net.

But the main concerns were centred on Clark who was immediately replaced by Hatters’ boss Jack Wilshere.



After the game, Luton revealed the player was responsive and sent to hospital as a precaution.

"We are able to update supporters on Jordan Clark’s condition following the clash of heads that resulted in him having to be carried off in the first half," a club statement read.



"After being taken to the dressing room, Jordan was responsive and talking to the medical team, but has been taken to hospital for further assessment.

"All our love and thoughts are with Clicker for a speedy recovery."

A flurry of goals in an entertaining 2-2 draw

The match burst into life in the latter stages of the first half with Nakhi Wells firing Luton in front from the penalty spot in the 41st minute.

But Luton were unable to hold onto their lead going into the interval as Callum Roberts equalised for the League One new boys.

Oliver Cooper gave the Magpies the lead on the hour but Luton dug deep to claim a point through Callum Marshall’s leveller eight minutes later.



Notts County, who kicked off the season with a 1-1 draw at home to Leicester City last week, took to social media to send Clark their best wishes.

The club wrote on X: “Sending our best wishes to Luton’s Jordan Clark, who is stretchered off with an injury sustained when making contact with the header.

“Darius Lipsiuc also required assessment after challenging Clark for the ball – but he’s OK to continue.”

2 The match at Kenilworth Road was halted for eight minutes so that medics could attend to Clark and Lipsiuc Credit: Getty



The result means both clubs remain unbeaten from their opening two matches.

Luton provisionally sit second in the table ahead of Saturday’s 3pm kick offs.

Meanwhile, Notts County have now registered two consecutive draws and occupy ninth place in League One.

Sports.title: Arsenal pushing for Julian Alvarez transfer with Atletico Madrid star set for late decision
Sports.content:
Arsenal pushing for Julian Alvarez transfer with Atletico Madrid star set for late decision

Arsenal are still actively exploring a move for Julian Alvarez before the transfer window closes, talkSPORT understands.

Sporting director Andrea Berta remains in talks with Alvarez and the Gunners have told Atletico Madrid they are ready to do business.

2 Alvarez's future remains up in the air with the window set to close on September 1 Credit: Getty

Atleti have repeatedly insisted that the Argentina forward is not for sale this summer and their preference is to keep him, but the player wants to leave.

Alvarez was left out of Diego Simeone's squad for the 2-0 victory over Malaga in LaLiga on Wednesday.

talkSPORT understands the former Manchester City star is yet to give the green light over a return to England.

Alvarez is keen to join Barcelona, but Atletico are reluctant to do business with their Spanish rivals, having already rejected an £86million bid and pointed towards his £432m release clause.

They were also left fuming by what appeared to be an insincere £129m bid from Real Madrid earlier this summer.

Atletico would much rather sell outside LaLiga if they decide to sanction a sale.

talkSPORT previously reported Arsenal have explored the idea of offering Viktor Gyokeres as a makeweight to sweeten the deal.

It means the decision rests with Alvarez - who has been left disappointed by Atleti's stance throughout the summer.

Tzolis shines on Arsenal debut

Arsenal showed their strength by cruising to a 3-0 win over Coventry City on the opening night of the Premier League.

Christos Tzolis impressed following a £34m move to the reigning champions earlier in the summer.

2 Tzolis looked the part on his Premier League debut Credit: Getty

He arrived days after Leandro Trossard completed a move to Turkish giants Besiktas.

Mikel Arteta's side missed out on Madrid superstar Vinicius Jr but remain overwhelming title favourites this season.

Left-winger Gabriel Martinelli, meanwhile, is linked with a move away from the Emirates before the window closes on September 1, having rejected a move to Galatasaray.

He was not named in the squad to face Coventry on Friday amid the links with an exit.

Before kick-off, Arsenal unveiled the £55m signing of Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa.

However, they were without fellow summer arrival Bruno Guimaraes, who is set for a spell on the sidelines with an injury.
