Why Canada suspended US trade talks despite Trump's 'good relationship' with Carney

Canada has suspended trade negotiations with the United States after Prime Minister Mark Carney rejected Washington's latest proposals as "unfair" and "uneconomic".

The move came after three days of intensive talks that had made progress on some tariffs but failed to resolve major differences over market access and retaliatory duties.

The US is preparing to impose tariffs of up to 50% on Canadian goods, while Carney said Canada would respond with matching tariffs, raising the risk of further disruption to deeply integrated North American supply chains.

Pakistan deploys army in Rawalpindi amid security concerns

Pakistan has authorised the deployment of three companies of the army in Rawalpindi for six months under Article 245 of the Constitution, following a request from the Punjab home department for "sensitive security duties". The move comes days after a shooting involving a man whom state-run media described as an active PTI member, though the party denied any connection to the incident.

The deployment is significant as Rawalpindi is home to the Pakistan Army's General Headquarters and is a key military and administrative centre.

World.title: People’s Watch expresses concern over surge in custodial torture cases
World.content:
People’s Watch, a human rights organisation based in Madurai, has expressed concern over the surge in custodial torture and death cases under the current administration.

Its Executive Director Henri Tiphagne said eight custodial death cases had been reported in Tamil Nadu within the completion of 100 days in office by the TVK-led government. In July alone, three custodial death cases had been reported. Last year, TVK leader C. Joseph Vijay spoke out against police violence. However, custodial deaths had increased since Mr. Vijay assumed office as Chief Minister.

State and the District Legal Services Authorities, State and District Police Complaints Authorities, and the Tamil Nadu State Human Rights Commission remained silent. “This situation is dangerous for our society,” he said.

The Tamil Nadu State Human Rights Commission had not taken suo motu cognisance of any of the recent cases since the TVK-led government came to power. Two member positions in SHRC and the post of Chairperson of the State Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes remained vacant.

He requested MLAs to raise the issues when the police demand for grants comes up for debate on September 3.

World.title: Commissioner seeks explanation from Joint Director of College Education over letter to principals of government colleges in T.N.
World.content:
The Commissioner of Collegiate Education has issued a showcause notice to the Joint Director (Planning and Development), Directorate of Collegiate Education, seeking an explanation for having sent a letter to principals of all government colleges directing them to take action to prevent students from participating in protests organised by Left parties and the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP).

The letter, which followed a directive from the Special Secretary of Higher Education that quoted minutes of a Law and Order meeting chaired by the Chief Secretary last month, had elicited considerable backlash from the Left parties, a coalition partner of the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) in the State, and the civil society.

In the showcause notice issued on Friday, the Commissioner noted that the Joint Director had acted on his own volition while sending the letter to principals of government arts and science colleges on August 17 and did not go through the Commissioner of Collegiate Education. The Joint Director has been given a week’s time to respond to the notice.

In the letter to the principals, the Joint Director had directed them to take action so as to prevent students from taking part in protests and agitations organised by the Left parties and the CJP and submit an action-taken report. After the issue snowballed into a controversy causing embarrassment to the government, the directive from the Special Secretary was withdrawn on August 19 prompting the Joint Director to withdraw the letter as well.

Meanwhile, the Tamil Nadu Government College Teachers’ Association (TNGCTA) has strongly condemned the explanation sought from the Joint Director of Collegiate Education. In a statement, S. Suresh, Secretary, TNGCTA, said that the Joint Director had sent the letter to the principals following the directive of the Special Secretary. The Registrar of University of Madras, too, had forwarded the same directive to all affiliated colleges. All these officials, the statement said, were carrying out orders from above. The statement also called for withdrawal of the showcause notice.

World.title: Congress says bulk applications to delete voter names are being processed in Uttarakhand
World.content:
UttarakhandCongress leaders have alleged that the Election Commission is accepting and processing unverified bulk applications to delete voters’ names during the claims and objections period of the ongoing special intensive revision (SIR) of voter lists in the State.

Also read | Uttarakhand begins pre-revision exercise to verify voters from 2003 rolls

The Congress submitted a memorandum to the Election Commission in Delhi on August 20, 2026, complaining that certain individuals have each submitted thousands of Form 7 applications. A party delegation subsequently met Uttarakhand’s Chief Electoral Officer B.V.R.C. Purushottam in Dehradun on August 21 to raise their concerns.

Form 7 is filed to object to an existing name on the electoral rolls or to request the deletion of a name due to reasons such as death, migration, or ineligibility. The booth-level officer (BLO) or the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) has to conduct an inquiry into each Form 7 application and issue a notice to the voter before taking any action.

‘Institutional access’

As The Hindu had earlier reported, such cases of bulk Form 7 submissions had previously surfaced in States such as Rajasthan, Gujarat and Assam. Most of the people in whose names the forms had been filed had denied that they had anything to do with them.

Congress leader Qazi Muhammed Nizamuddin, who represents the Manglaur constituency in the Uttarakhand Assembly, was part of the delegation to the ECI. The MLA alleged that the manner in which the bulk forms were submitted online pointed to “institutional” access being granted to some organisation.

The Uttarakhand CEO Mr. Purushottam told The Hindu that he would look into all such allegations of bulk Form 7 submissions in the State.

Mandatory review

While booth-level agents of political parties are allowed to file up to 10 Form 7s a day, with a total of 30, there is no limit on how many such forms an individual can submit.

However, ECI sources said that, to prevent misuse of the process, if a person files more than five objections, it will trigger a mandatory review by the ERO to ensure the legitimacy of the claims.

The Congress memorandum claimed that several Form 7 objections in Uttarakhand have been filed by people who are not electors from, or in any other way connected with, the concerned Assembly Constituency.

It added that, according to the rules, the ERO has to conduct a summary inquiry and record a decision, with both the objector and the person objected to entitled to appear and be heard. However, in practice, this dual-notice requirement is not being observed, and in most cases, the objector is not present in the hearings, the memorandum said.

One man files thousands of objections

According to a Congress analysis of Form-10 data (the register of claims and objections) issued by the office of the Uttarakhand CEO for all Assembly constituencies, from the date of voter list draft publication up to August 6, a total of 262 individual objectors have each filed more than 10 Form 7 objections; between them, these 262 people alone have lodged several thousand objections seeking the deletion of electors.

The party offered the example of Kichha Assembly constituency in Udham Singh Nagar district where one individual, Rajesh Tiwari, is stated to have submitted approximately 6,410 objections.

The Congress letter also said that unannounced exercises have restarted to identify demographically or photo similar entries, proposing the deletion of 102,793 electors in Udham Singh Nagar district alone, without any proper written guidelines or due notice.

The draft electoral rolls of the State were published on July 14, with the final list scheduled to be released on September 15. The claims and objections period was open till August 13, and the disposal of notices will take place till September 11.

World.title: BJP passes resolution against Congress over Vande Mataram issue, steps up Gen-Z outreach
World.content:
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Saturday (August 22, 2026) passed a resolution criticising the Congress Working Committee’s decision to reaffirm its 1937 resolution and restrict the singing of Vande Mataram to its first two stanzas at Congress events. The party also stepped up preparations for a nationwide Gen-Z outreach programme.

BJP president Nitin Nabin held his first meeting with the newly-appointed national office-bearers, which was also attended by their predecessors. In the evening, Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed the new team.

“Organisational meetings are all about new ideas and perspectives aimed at strengthening the Party and deepening connect with the people. Great interaction with fellow Party colleagues and the new organisational team!” said Mr. Modi on X. During the meeting, the Prime Minister exhorted the office-bearers to intensify the outreach to the young generation.

Focus on youth

The day’s meetings focused on strengthening the BJP’s connect with the people, particularly the younger generation. The party decided to constitute a team for its upcoming nationwide Gen-Z outreach programme, focused on understanding the aspirations and concerns of the younger generation. It is likely to include Mr. Nabin, national general secretaries Smriti Irani and Vinod Tawde, Gujarat Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi, and Chhattisgarh Minister O.P. Choudhary.

Another meeting focused on the decision to run a month-long programme across the country from September 17 to October 17, marking Mr. Modi’s birthday and 25 years since he became Gujarat Chief Minister.

In its 10-point resolution on Vande Mataram, the BJP rejected what it described as attempts to subordinate the song to communal pressure, political appeasement or vote-bank politics. The party said the Congress Working Committee’s 1937 decision could not override constitutional institutions or laws.

It resolved to “affirm the constitutional and statutory status of Vande Mataram as established by the Constituent Assembly’s 1950 pronouncement and reinforced by Parliament’s 2026 amendment [the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Act] extending statutory protection to the National Song equivalent to that accorded to the National Anthem”.

National campaign

The BJP announced a nationwide campaign through its workers to educate people, particularly the youth, about the National Song’s history, six-stanza composition and national significance.

“That legacy cannot be reduced to the calculations of contemporary vote-bank politics. The same ‘Vande Mataram’ that echoed as the call for freedom in 1947 will resound as the supreme chant for a ‘Developed India @ 2047’ under the vision of Prime Minister Narendra Modi,” it said.

At a press conference, BJP MP Sambit Patra referred to a complaint filed with the police seeking registration of a case to probe alleged “intentional obstruction/disturbance” during the rendition of the National Song at the All India Congress Committee headquarters on August 15.

Mr. Patra said the recently enacted Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Act prescribed imprisonment and a fine, and that the law would take its course.

Addressing the media, BJP national general secretary Vinod Tawde shared details of the first meeting of the national office-bearers and the workshop organised for the month-long ‘Seva Sankalp Abhiyan’.

The campaign will include service-oriented initiatives such as honouring Anganwadi workers and organising ‘Matri Samvad’ events. Under ‘Seva Setu’, block-level camps will help eligible beneficiaries enrol in government welfare schemes. Youth will be encouraged to showcase service activities, while a National Innovation Challenge will seek solutions to local problems. State, district and block-level workshops will be held to take the programme to the grassroots.

World.title: Uneven utility patches add to motorists’ woes in Tambaram
World.content:
Motorists and schoolchildren in several parts of Tambaram City Corporation are facing a fresh hazard on roads already affected by potholes and damaged surfaces: uneven patches laid after roads are dug up for water supply and underground drainage (UGD) works.

In several locations, the excavated portions have been restored with concrete, but the surface has not been brought back to its original level. Two-wheeler riders and cyclists are forced to suddenly change direction to avoid the rough patches, while motorists have to slow down and manoeuvre around them, affecting the smooth flow of traffic.

A visit to several roads from Pallavaram to Tambaram showed that the problem was particularly acute at a number of locations. Here are six trouble spots:

Driving along Sivasankaran Street near Pallavaram railway station towards the flyover leading to Shandy Road has become difficult. The approach to the flyover has several uneven and damaged portions, forcing motorists to move towards either edge of the carriageway to avoid the rough surface. Sudden U-turns by autorickshaws and vehicles from the service road add to the risk. There is also a lack of clarity over whether the affected portion comes under Tambaram Corporation or the Cantonment Board. Corporation Commissioner S. Balachandran said he would look into the issue.

Railway Border Road, popularly known as Vaishnava College Border Road, is used by hundreds of motorists to Tirusulam towards the Metro station or seeking to avoid GST Road congestion. A portion of the road, which was laid about six months ago, was dug up last month for pipe-laying work. Though it was subsequently filled and restored with concrete, the patch remains uneven. With the road already narrow, two-wheeler riders tend to avoid the affected portion.

On Chitlapakkam Main Road, a stretch from the R.P. Road junction was recently dug up for laying water pipelines and restored with concrete. While several patches are manageable, the stretch diagonally opposite Varadaraja Cinemas near the autorickshaw stand remains particularly uneven. Street vendors said two-wheeler riders, including women, had lost balance while negotiating the patch.

Ayyasamy School Street in Ward 35, Chromepet, located between the MTC depot, a petrol bunk, several schools and the MIT campus, has also been dug up at multiple points for drinking water pipeline work. The uneven surfaces have made cycling difficult for school students. Saranya, a student, said her bicycle had suffered punctures at least twice in the past fortnight while using the road.

The Agaram Main Road near the Camp Road junction in Ward 45, Tambaram, presents a different problem. A portion of the road is covered with sand and mud in connection with the Chennai Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board’s Nemmeli Seawater Desalination Project. A mound of mud in the middle of the road poses a risk to motorists, particularly school and college students. Councillor ‘Kodi’ Dhamodharan said concrete patches were being laid on a priority basis and that the road would be re-laid soon.

At the Thiruporur Road-Hasthinapuram bus stand junction, encroachments have already reduced the available road space. A large pothole at the junction makes it difficult for motorists, pedestrians and school and office-goers to negotiate the stretch.

Munusamy, a long-time resident, said several minor accidents caused by the poor road condition went unreported. “Before any major tragedy occurs, the Corporation should prioritise blacktopping the roads to ensure motorists’ safety,” he said.

Corporation Commissioner’s response

Corporation Commissioner S. Balachandran said the cost of road works and shortage of bitumen were among the factors affecting full-scale blacktopping. Concrete patches, he said, were being laid on a priority basis as an immediate solution to ensure the continuous movement of vehicles.

“Instead of waiting for blacktopping, concrete mix is done to ensure continuous free flow of vehicle movement, taking into account the traffic mobility of the road,” he said.

On complaints about uneven surfaces, he said defects would be rectified if brought to the Corporation’s notice. He also appealed to the public to wait until the cement had dried fully before using the repaired portions, as movement over the wet surface could leave impressions and result in uneven patches.

Meanwhile, cracks have reportedly developed on the MIT flyover roundabout. S.M. Govindarajan, founder-president of the United Federation of Residents’ Welfare Associations under Tambaram Corporation, said the Highways Department had filled the cracks with concrete or bitumen instead of relaying the affected portion fully.

He also pointed to a large crater-like depression on the downward slope of the Pallavaram-Thoraipakkam flyover on GST Road east, which he said had become accident-prone.

“I myself skidded twice on the stretch. When contacted, the Highways Department said a new tender would be called,” he said.

Residents and activists urged the Corporation and Highways Department to adopt better restoration methods for roads dug up for pipelines and other development works, instead of relying on temporary measures.

World.title: Infant dead, two injured in fire at NICU in Madhya Pradesh’s Chhindwara
World.content:
An infant was killed and two other newborns suffered burn injuries after a fire broke out in the neonatal ICU (NICU) at the government district hospital in Madhya Pradesh’s Chhindwara, officials said on Saturday (August 22, 2026). Officials said the deceased newborn was a girl child who had a congenital heart condition.

According to officials, the incident took place around 1.50 a.m. after a radiant warmer machine in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit caught fire due to sparks in its filament coil, causing injuries to three children. In an NICU, newborns who are in poor health at birth would be placed on the beds attached to the machine, which keeps them warm.

The district administration has ordered an investigation into the incident and the civil surgeon will probe the cause behind the fire.

Hospital in-charge and civil surgeon Kanchan Dubey said that after an initial examination, the three infants were referred to the government medical college in Jabalpur.

“There were a total of 33 children there [in the NICU] and these three [infants] were placed on the same warmer. Our staff, including nurses, acted with promptness and saved the other 30 children. They were initially moved to another unit and after technicians and electricians inspected all other machines, the children were shifted back to the NICU,” she said, terming the tragedy an accident and denied any negligence on part of the hospital staff.

“The administrative officials will come and conduct an investigation but I don’t see any negligence in this. It is an accident,” she said, adding that the fire was quickly doused.

Dr. Dubey also denied any technical fault in the machine and said that it was on annual maintenance.

No paediatric surgeon

District hospital paediatrician Anshul Lamba said that the children were referred to the facility in Jabalpur as there was no paediatric surgeon at the hospital. “After the primary treatment, surgical inspection was conducted by specialists and opinion was taken. Since, we do not have a paediatric surgeon here, they were sent to Jabalpur for better treatment,” Dr. Lamba said.

“There was a short circuit in the coil. It did not happen anywhere in the electrical line; the short circuit occurred only in the coil. The problem is that the oxygen tubing also runs from that very area. The short circuit produced sparks, which fell on the oxygen tubing, and caused fire in the cradle. The staff managed to bring out the three children from the cradle within 15 seconds but due to the foam mattress, they suffered burn injuries,” he said.

Speaking to The Hindu, Chhindwara Collector Harendra Narayan Mishra said that an investigation has been ordered into the matter and the civil surgeon will probe the cause of the incident.

“I have been told by the hospital administration that the machine had undergone its annual maintenance on August 10 and no fault had been detected. But since a tragedy has happened, we have informed the maintenance agency in Bhopal. Their engineers will visit the hospital soon for an inspection,” he said.

Mr. Mishra said that the deceased girl child was born with dextrocardia, a congenital condition in which the child’s heart is on the right side of the chest. The doctors said that the other two newborns were also born with serious conditions, with one of them suffering congenital diaphragmatic hernia, a surgical condition.

Injured infants stable

“I spoke to the Medical Superintendent in the evening and the other two children are stable,” he said.

Mr. Mishra said that there were a total of 63 infants in the NICU — 30 in the inborn unit and 33 in the outborn unit, where the tragedy took place, and that there were only 27 warmer machines available, forcing the hospital administration to accommodate two or three children in one cradle.

“Government hospitals usually receive heavy footfall and since most patients are from rural or poor backgrounds, the hospital has to accommodate them all,” he said.

Room full of smoke: kin

Roopmal Verma, a relative of the deceased girl child, narrated the scene to the media saying that the families had initially been told that all children were safe and shifted to another ward.

“I was among the first to reach the spot and the room was filled with smoke. Later, we were told on the phone that our child had suffered burns and will be referred to Jabalpur. She was born around 10.30 [on Friday] night. There is so much negligence here. The nursing staff even asks for money [from families] saying that they will do the delivery properly,” he said.

Anand Verma, relative of another affected child, alleged negligence on part of the hospital staff and administration.

Chhindwara’s public health infrastructure was under criticism last year after 25 children died of kidney failure due to consumption of an adulterated cough syrup manufactured in Tamil Nadu. At the time, most of the affected children had to be admitted in public and private hospitals in Maharashtra’s Nagpur due to lack of necessary infrastructure in Chhindwara even as the local administration remained clueless about the deaths for weeks.

In November 2024, at least 17 infants were killed in Uttar Pradesh’s Jhansi after a massive fire broke out at the NICU of State-run Maharani Laxmi Bai Medical College Hospital.

World.title: Badminton World Championships: Treesa and Gayatri’s giant-kiling spree comes to an end
World.content:
It was a dream run that had to end at some point. Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand, giant-killers who accounted for higher-ranked opponents at the badminton World Championships in New Delhi, finally ran out of steam in the semifinals, going down fighting to China’s Sheng Shu Liu & Ning Tan 18-21, 21-13, 21-8 as the Indian challenge ended on the penultimate day on Saturday (August 22, 2026).

The match started with the Chinese as firm favourites. However, the match took the players and the fans alike through a roller-coaster of fortunes and emotions. Eventually, the Chinese duo, who are the top seeds, reigning World champions and runners-up at the Paris Olympics two years ago, advanced to the final.

The Indians, already assured of a medal, lost, but were not discredited. If anything, the performance only burnished their growing reputation as serious challengers. Starting slow, the Indians relied more on skills and smart play than raw power to race to a 7-2 lead before Sheng and Ning reiterated why they are so feared on the circuit.

The Chinese reeled off 10 consecutive points to go 12-7 up, increasing the pace of the game and with some impeccable placement and it looked like it would be yet another straight game win for them before Treesa and Gayatri decided they would not give up so easily.

The Indians had played a different game to their previous outings so far, relying more on cross-court volleys and soft drops at the net instead. The match took a turn as the Indians came out all guns blazing and used their jump smashes to pick up six consecutive points and go 13-12 up. The match was even-stevens till Liu dropped her service short at 16-18, and the game ended 16-18 in favour of the Indians. This was also the first game that the Chinese pair had dropped in the tournament.

The Chinese defence was impenetrable, the players retrieving shuttles sometimes barely inches from the floor. Coupled with targeting the Indians’ bodies and increased aggression, Sheng and Tan gave no breathing space.

The second game, too, stayed close till 12-12 before the Chinese took off eight points to close at 21-13 and then raced away in the decider.

Korea’s Baek Ha Na and Lee So Hee beat Li Yi Jing and Luo Xu Min 21-17, 21-12 in the other semifinal.

Meanwhile, Akane Yamaguchi will face An Se-young for her title defence, the two top-ranked players in women’s badminton setting up their 35th encounter on the circuit with straight-game wins in their respective semifinals. While Yamaguchi beat Pornpawee Chochuwong 21-12, 21-17, Se-young had a relatively tougher fight against Wang Zhiyi before prevailing 24-22, 21-16 to extend her record against the Chinese 21-5.

Lanier makes history

Alex Lanier became the first Frenchman ever to reach the title clash of the marquee event with a 16-21, 21-13, 21-14 win against Victor Lai of Canada. He will take on Kodai Naraoka after the latter beat Chou Tien Chen 17-21, 21-11, 21-10.

The results (semifinals): Men: Alex Lanier (Fra) bt Victor Lai (Can) 16-21, 21-13, 21-14; Kodai Naraoka (Jpn) bt Chou Tien Chen (Tpe) 17-21, 21-11, 21-10.

Doubles: Aaron Chia & Soh Wooi Yik (Mas) bt Kim Won Ho & Seo Seung Jae (Kor) 21-17, 21-18; Liang Wei Keng & Wang Chang (Chn) bt Lee Jhe-Huei & Yang Po-Hsuan (Tpe) 21-18, 21-14.

Women: Akane Yamaguchi (Jpn) bt Pornpawee Chochuwong (Tha) 21-12, 21-17; An Se-young (Kor) bt Wang Zhiyi (Chn) 24-22, 21-16;.

Doubles: Baek Ha Na & Lee So Hee (Kor) bt Li Yi Jing & Luo Xu Min (Chn) 21-17, 21-12; Sheng Shu Liu & Ning Tan (Chn) bt Treesa Jolly & Gayatri Gopichand 18-21, 21-13, 21-8.

Mixed doubles: Feng Yan Zhe & Huang Dong Ping (Chn) bt Amri Syahnawi & Nita Violina Marwah (Ina) 20-22, 21-14, 22-20; Thom Gicquel & Delphine Delrue (Fra) bt Jiang Zheng Bang & Wei Ya Xin 19-21, 21-13, 21-11.

World.title: I’ve got my eye on you
World.content:
Two weeks ago, I watched a video on X (formerly Twitter) of a man using AI to digitally undress a hijab-wearing Muslim woman on an Indian train. After clicking pictures of her, his simple one-line command could sexualise her on his device and strip her image of clothes and dignity. The person who recorded the video complained to the Railway Police, who then trashed him. Even watching the video sent shivers down my spine because I knew that I could be at the receiving end of a crime as heinous as this.

Poet-author Meena Kandasamy, whose book Fieldwork as a Sex Object deals with this issue, spoke at an event conducted by The Hindu on August 21. She said women’s agency does not exist any more, especially since big tech is inherently misogynistic. The concept of bodily autonomy, particularly for women, has ceased to exist, she said, making the world even scarier than it already is. Kandasamy herself has battled a decade of online trolling, so much so that she has often been been subjected to rape threats for her opinions.

An article in The Hindu about deepfakes and its misuse says AI-generated pornographic clips cause victims to deal with shame, trauma, and judgment, sometimes even from those closest to them. “What’s even more heartbreaking is that proving a video is fake doesn’t always fix the damage. Once something is out there, it spreads fast and the Internet rarely forgets,” writes Nehal Saxena.

A report in The New York Times published in January this year said that over nine days, Elon Musk’s Grok chatbot generated and posted 4.4 million images, of which at least 41% were sexualised images of women. In that time period, 1.8 million nude images of women were created on the site.

Seema Anand, a London-based author and creator who often speaks about sex education in her videos, filed an FIR regarding a number of AI-generated sexual images of her. The 63-year-old posted a video saying the incident made her feel “physically sick”.

What, then, is the solution for women who already face real-life physical threats, including stalking?

According to Tech Policy Press, 61 countries’ data protection and privacy authorities across four continents have put AI image-generation companies on notice, declaring that nonconsensual intimate imagery is a privacy violation, and regulators intend to act on it. In India, under the Digital Data Protection Act, 2023, the circulation of non-consensual sexual content is prohibited, but generation is not.

Nehal says technology must be created by big tech to counter deepfakes, and stronger laws are essential. She also advocates for digital literacy for young students in schools and colleges.

But the truth is that this is not enough. Women do not need to have a digital presence to experience such extreme violation.

WORDSWORTH

Oocyte cryopreservation: U.S. Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez has been posting videos on the Internet about women freezing their eggs. Oocyte cryopreservation is a process where a woman’s eggs are taken from her ovaries, flash-frozen using a method called vitrification, and stored at very cold temperatures for future use. Cortez, who has been seen in a video injecting herself with medication just before a TV interview, says that she was doing it “to show more depictions of women having full lives in every context and every choice.” She intends to freeze her eggs, keeping in mind her demanding political career. She also says that there are double standards in politics because women face intrusive questions regarding age and family planning, whereas men in similar public roles do not.

TOOLKIT

A two-day photography fellowship for women called Kanavu by the Chennai Photo Biennale is aimed at equipping them with the skills to become visual storytellers. On August 29 and 30, a two-day workshop in Madurai will be conducted to ensure that women wielding the camera become more confident. It first began in 2022 and has already benefitted several women, particularly from small towns, like Theni-based Chandini Ramesh who runs a baby photography venture called The Little Bud Photography. Read this article for all the details.

OUCH!

“But is it about the training? Because I think that for women, it’s more like, climbing on the rock and climbing maybe on the lead, for doing it as a hobby, it’s quite fun, and lots of women [are] doing it. But when you go into the world class, you need to go to the gym, you need to train with weights, and all that stuff, and this is more the ‘boy thing,’ right?”

Austrian sports commentator Claudio Sunk at the World Climbing Europe Youth Series in St. Pölten

Thirupurasundari Sevvel, architect and historian, who has curated, along with The Hindu’s library team, The Hindu’s archival photo exhibit titled Madras On Stage is a big proponent of women telling their own tales. In her organisation, Nam Veedu Nam Oor Nam Kadhai, a history collective which conducts heritage walks, there is a focus on women who make history. “This is clearly intentional. They make up half my team,” she says. The photo exhibit in the office premises tends to have a wall dedicated to women and their achievements. “There is a definite gender-gap in pictures taken of women in historical archives but that does not mean we will stop hunting for their stories,” she says. The archival photo exhibit is on till September 10.

World.title: Govt blames PTI for 'violating' SC order, says family committed contempt by issuing statements
World.content:
The government on Saturday blamed the PTI for “violating” a Supreme Court (SC) order by issuing statements and speaking to the media following former prime minister Imran Khan’s medical check-up at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) on Friday.

“PML-N believes that health issues should not be used for political gain,” Information Minister Attaullah Tarar told the media.

He added that, whether in opposition or in government, the PML-N’s stance had always remained the same: politics and health issues should not be linked.

The minister also accused Imran of issuing statements and releasing videos about the health of PML-N leaders when they were incarcerated and he was prime minister.

Tarar added that since the SC order regarding Imran’s health was issued, “our government has not mocked him or made any controversial statements”.

Recounting events of the past few days, Tarar said that after the SC order was issued, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar had explained the government’s position on it in detail.

“The viewpoint was that whatever will happen, it will be according to the law,” Tarar said.

He added that the government’s review petition “respectfully questioned whether the facility was available to every prisoner”. Secondly, he said, the petition questioned whether the law and Constitution allowed Imran to be examined at a private hospital.

Tarar then elaborated on the implementation of the SC’s order.

“The next question is whether the order was implemented. The answer is yes. Was the check-up conducted? Yes. Was it done transparently? Yes. Was his sister present? Yes. Were doctors from Shifa [Hospital] present? Yes. All the obligations were fulfilled.”

Tarar also addressed the communication of these developments to the media and the general public. He said that shortly after the government filed its review petition, the law minister had explained its grounds in detail.

He added that after Imran’s check-up was completed at Pims, he himself posted an update on X.

Tarar said he was “surprised” by the PTI’s subsequent statements and actions. “PTI is miles away from the light of knowledge,” he said, adding that the party would not have filed a contempt petition had it been aware of the situation.

“A baseless contempt petition has been filed.”

The facts were shared with the public immediately, he said, adding that the government had maintained transparency throughout.

“Contempt has definitely happened,” he said, adding that the SC had directed that no political motives should be involved in the medical check-up. However, Tarar said, people gathered outside Shifa Hospital, created social media content and removed barriers.

“Wasn’t it the PTI that did this? Didn’t they violate the court order?”

He added that the PTI had also issued statements and spoken at press conferences.

“If somebody is in contempt, it is Imran Khan’s sister and his party.

“The prisoner’s family was in contempt. His party was in contempt by gathering people and creating problems for the authorities.”

He remarked that this was the first time a political party had created problems for its own founder’s health and treatment.

Tarar added that earlier the Pakistan Bar Council and Punjab Bar Council had issued statements saying that some lawyers associated with the two bodies were, in their personal capacities, issuing statements to politicise the matter. Both councils had clarified that the bar councils should be kept separate from the issue, he said.

“Some lawyers have tried to pollute bar politics,” Tarar said.

Eight members of the Pakistan Bar Council (PBC) on Saturday strongly condemned the government’s “blatant, wilful and deliberate violation” of the SC’s Aug 18 order.

“The order of the SC was clear, unequivocal and binding yet the executive has chosen to disregard it and has acted in direct defiance of the court’s directions and violated the same,” said a statement issued by the members.

Meanwhile, Vice Chairman of the PBC Pir Muhammad Masood Chistie clarified that the statement represented the views of those individual members and could not be treated as the collective position of the PBC.

“You obstructed his path. You created a security situation there,” the minister said, addressing PTI leadership.

He added that the medical report from Pims had stated that Imran was in good health, prompting the question: “Which illness are you doing politics on?”

Imran’s medical treatment had never been stopped or paused and would continue as needed, the information asserted, urging PTI leaders and Imran’s family not to politicise legal or health matters, adding that they had “been in contempt” by commenting on the issue.

Tarar issued the statement hours after Dr Uzma Khan, Imran’s sister, approached the SC seeking to initiate contempt proceedings against those responsible for violating its Aug 18 order to shift the incarcerated former premier to a private hospital in the federal capital.

On Tuesday, the SC had ordered the government to shift Imran to Shifa International Hospital within two days for examination and treatment by a multidisciplinary medical board.

The court had also ordered that Dr Uzma Khan and Dr Faisal Sultan — Imran’s personal physician — be present during the medical examination by the board. At the same time, Imran’s family members, PTI members and lawyers associated with him were barred from disclosing his health condition or medical reports to the media or the public until the next hearing.

The next day, the government had filed a review plea against the court’s order to shift Imran to the private hospital, arguing that the directive was discriminatory and issued in violation of prison rules and principles of natural justice.

However, the SC had returned the plea on Thursday with the objection that the contents of the affidavit and facts, along with the review petition filed under Article 188 of the Constitution, had not been properly drawn up and that one of the paper books of was not in order.

The same night, elaborate arrangements were put in place in and around Shifa International Hospital, and all signs pointed to the PTI founder being brought there, in compliance with SC order.

However, it became clear on Friday morning that Imran had been taken to Pims for a check-up and then subsequently transported back to prison.

World.title: 'Completely choreographed drama': PTI's Salman Akram Raja slams govt over failure to follow SC order
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: PTI General Secretary Salman Akram Raja on Saturday accused the federal government of carrying out a “completely choreographed drama” and dishonouring the Supreme Court’s directive to transfer party founder Imran Khan to Shifa International Hospital.

Speaking to Geo News, he discussed the contempt of court petition filed by Advocate Uzair Karamat Bhandari, who represents Imran’s sister, Dr Uzma Khan, seeking to initiate contempt proceedings against those responsible for violating the SC’s Aug 18 order to shift the incarcerated premier to a private hospital in the federal capital.

The PTI secretary general emphasised that filing the petition was not a political move but “a purely legal and professional decision”.

“We have named jail administrators, the Punjab interior secretary, government officials and ministers, and the prime minister,” Raja said. “It was a professional decision taken by Dr Uzma Khan’s lawyer after taking the situation into account.”

He added that he spoke with Bhandari about the plea, who told him that it is necessary to name officeholders and the premier as parties in the case.

“The matter will be discussed in court, but regardless, the Supreme Court’s decision was not honoured. Nothing was implemented: there was no transfer to Shifa, there was no [medical] board with Dr Uzma and Dr Faisal Sultan and there was supposed to be treatment. None of this happened; there was only a few hours of drama,” Raja explained.

“There was no road closure or security threat,” he added. “A convoy departed Adiala jail and went to Shifa International, taking Dr Faisal Sultan. People thought it was Khan sahib. This is a completely choreographed drama.”

However, Raja noted that an administrative official is unable to unilaterally disregard an order from the apex court, and that the truth would expose who decided to ignore it.

Asked why Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi was not named as a party, Raja said the plea was not a party matter but a decision taken by Bhandari in his capacity as Dr Uzma’s lawyer.

“If Mohsin Naqvi is not involved in the decision-making or if there is no evidence of his involvement, then he has not been named as a party,” he responded.

“In [a case of] contempt of court, it is essential that the people whom you are accusing made the decision to disobey the court or had a part in it. Whoever they are, and if any new evidence comes forward, we can do that (name party),” Raja added, reiterating that the plea was “purely a professional decision”.

Asked if Naqvi was not named because he tried to implement the court order, Raja said neither he nor Bhandari had any knowledge of that and that upon asking the latter, he said he took the decision based on the documented evidence available.

He noted, however, that the interior secretary could take many decisions on their own, which was why Bhandari named the head of the government as a party.

Raja also rejected claims that the plea would have been heard by the court immediately had it been filed yesterday, calling them “incorrect and baseless”.

“When something is filed with the Supreme Court, it isn’t slated for hearing immediately,” he explained.

“Secondly, this incident took place at night. Dr Uzma returned at 6am and got in contact with Bhandari sahib at 9am. He got to work, but he could not file anything after 11am on a Friday. Even if it were filed, it would be heard by next week at the earliest, and it will be the same for this case.”

Contempt of court plea

The petition, moved by Advocate Bhandari, also requested the SC to depute an officer of the court or appoint a local commission to ensure that Imran was immediately shifted to Shifa International Hospital for his medical examination in accordance with the Aug 18 order.

Islamabad Chief Commissioner Islamabad, (retired) Lieutenant Sohail Ashraf, Interior Secretary Ahmed Raza Sarwar, Punjab Inspector General Prisons Mian Salik Jalal, Adiala Jail Superintendent Sajid Baig, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar and Information Minister Attaullah Tarar were named as respondents in the petition.

While all eyes were on Shifa International Hospital, a private medical facility, during the early hours of Friday, the government quietly moved Imran to the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) for a medical check-up in, ostensibly due to security concerns, following which he was taken back to Adiala jail.

The PTI leadership and Uzma, who was present for the medical examination, had slammed the government’s conduct.

The contempt plea filed by Uzma on Saturday urged the SC to initiate contempt proceedings against the respondents for their “wilful, deliberate and contumacious disobedience and violation” of the Aug 18 order.

The petition contended that the court was being approached in light of the “non-compliance and brazen violations” by the respondents of the SC’s orders.

“It is clear from the respondents’ own admissions that the court directions contained in Aug 18 order were violated,” it said.

“The directions contained in the Aug 18 orders were clear, unambiguous, unequivocal and fully capable of implementation,” the petition said, adding they were issued in the presence of the Islamabad advocate general and the additional attorney general of Pakistan.

“No portion thereof requires any further interpretation, clarification or modification,” the petition argued. It said that the respondents, being the officials responsible for putting the directions into effect, were under an absolute legal obligation to comply with the order “in letter and spirit”.

“Needless to say, the mere filing of a review petition on the part of the chief commissioner does not affect the legal status of the court order and does not justify non-compliance with it,” the plea said.

It said that even if a clarification or modification was required or there was apprehension of a security situation, an application needed to be filed.

It said that the failure to shift Imran to Shifa International Hospital “leaves no manner of doubt that [the respondents] have consciously chosen to disregard and violate the Aug 18 court order”.

It said that this was a case of deliberate and wilful disobedience and a violation of the order, interference with the process of law and obstruction of the judicial process.

The petition said that the respondents’ conduct undermined the authority of the SC, adding that such conduct warranted cognisance by the court.

The petition requested the SC to issue show-cause notices to the respondents and direct them to appear personally.

The petition also requested to impose appropriate punishments against the respondents and direct to take all appropriate steps to implement the directions contained in the Aug 18 order for Imran’s medical examination.

Imran’s hospital transfer saga

On Tuesday, the SC had ordered the government to shift Imran to Shifa International Hospital within two days for examination and treatment by a multidisciplinary medical board.

A three-member bench headed by Justice Shahid Waheed and comprising Justices Naeem Akhtar Afghan and Ishtiaq Ibr­ahim issued the interim directions on petitions seeking Imran’s hospitalisation, access to personal physicians and family members and provision of his medical record to his family.

The court had also ordered that Dr Uzma Khan and Dr Faisal Sultan — Imran Khan’s personal physician — be present during the medical check-up by a medical board.

At the same time, Imran’s family members, PTI members and lawyers associated with him were barred from disclosing his health condition or medical reports to the media or public until the next hearing.

The next day, the government had filed a review plea against the court’s order to shift Imran to the private hospital, arguing that the directive was discriminatory and issued in violation of prison rules and principles of natural justice.

However, the SC had returned the plea on Thursday with the objection that the contents of the affidavit and facts, along with the review petition filed under Article 188 of the Constitution, had not been properly drawn up and that one of the paper books of was not in order.

The same night, elaborate arrangements were put in place in and around Shifa International Hospital, and all signs pointed to the PTI founder being brought there, in compliance with SC order.

However, it became clear on Friday morning that Imran had been taken to Pims for a check-up and then subsequently transported back to prison.

Information Minister Attaullah Tarar blamed “the security situation created by PTI workers on the way to and outside Al Shifa Hospital” for the diversion.

In a post on X, he said, “In the light of the SC’s order, the prisoner was taken to the hospital under appropriate security arrangements during the night between August 20 and 21.

“A team of qualified doctors, including an ophthalmologist, a cardiologist, and a physician, conducted a detailed examination of him and declared him medically fit,” he said.

Later, the Pims administration said that two specialists from Shifa Inter­national Hospital participated in Imran’s eye assessment, while other exa­minations were carri­­ed out by the concerned Pims specialists.

Imran has been taken to Pims multiple times after his eye ailment — right central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO) — came to light in late January.

“The clinical input ari­sing from the ophthalmological assessment was taken into account alongside findings of the investigations conducted at Pims,” the statement said.

Meanwhile, the government on Thursday filed a fresh review petition against the SC’s Aug 18 order. The Islamabad chief commissioner again filed the plea, saying that his office had a direct, substantial and legally protected interest in the matter and that the Aug 18 order adversely affected its constitutional authority.

World.title: PM Shehbaz takes notice of non-functional CTA machine at PIMS cardiology dept; Imran's related test not performed
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday took notice of the non-functional computed tomography angiography (CTA) machine at the cardiology department of the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims), after former premier Imran Khan was brought to the hospital for a medical check-up.

The premier has constituted a committee, headed by the Establishment Division secretary, to examine all aspects of the matter, determine the facts and fix responsibility.

According to a senior doctor who is part of the medical facility’s administration, the lapse occurred after the PTI founder was brought to the hospital in the early hours of Friday without prior intimation, referral or patient registration.

“Ideally, Imran Khan should have been brought in daylight, as it was not an emergency case, and he should have been registered as a patient. All departments were not in the loop,” he told Dawn.

According to credible sources at Pims, who requested anonymity, Imran’s CTA — commonly known as CT angiography — was recommended, but the test could not be completed because the facility was unavailable. Imran was subsequently taken back to Adiala jail.

On Friday, after it emerged that Imran’s CTA could not be conducted at Pims, some senior doctors said the required machine was available in the radiology department, but the information was not brought to the attention of those treating Imran while he was at the hospital.

The CTA machine at the Cardiac Centre had been available in 2011 but later became non-functional, the doctors said.

A senior doctor added that the Cardiac Centre had a facility for conventional angiography, in which a vein is punctured and a camera is used to diagnose a blockage. The functional CTA machine, however, was available only in the radiology department, the doctor added.

Another doctor reiterated that the CTA machine in the radiology department had been functional since March 2022.

“The CTA is performed by a radiologist on the advice of clinicians as it uses radiation rather than requiring a vein to be punctured. However, no one advised that Imran be referred to the radiology department,” he said.

He further told Dawn that after the matter came to light, Health Secretary Muhammad Aslam Ghauri visited Pims and verified that the machine was available.

A senior Pims administrator, who requested anonymity, said cardiologists were asked about the test but told officials that the facility was unavailable. As a result, it was conveyed that Imran Khan’s CTA could not be conducted.

“The fact is that most CTAs are referred to private facilities because the machine at the Cardiac Centre is out of order. When the issue was raised on Saturday, the radiology department was asked to provide records of CTAs conducted there. It provided just one report, while claiming that around a dozen others were also available,” he said.

The officer, who has administrative responsibilities, said he had been receiving requests from the Cardiac Centre for years to arrange a machine, so no one considered referring Imran to the radiology department.

“Moreover, cardiologists used to conduct CTAs themselves in the past, so they are not accustomed to referring patients to the radiology department,” he explained.

According to an official government statement, the premier took notice of the non-functional CTA facility at Pims and constituted an inquiry committee to determine the facts.

The premier directed the committee to examine all aspects of the matter and submit a report.

The committee may co-opt any other member if required.

The committee will investigate the coordination and referral mechanisms between the cardiology and radiology departments and assess the role of the hospital administration in providing the facility.

It will also examine whether patients in the cardiology department were routinely referred to private medical centres for CTA.

In cases of such referrals, the committee will determine whether any particular private facility was given preference and how much business was diverted from the public hospital to private centres.

The inquiry committee will further investigate any lack of coordination, mismanagement or misunderstanding between the cardiology and radiology departments that may have resulted in a loss to the public interest and identify the officers or offices responsible.

PM Shehbaz directed the committee to conduct a comprehensive examination of all relevant facts and records and submit its report so that further action could be taken in accordance with the law.
